def run(cmd):
    return subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)


def kinetic(binary, model, prompt, repetitions):
    out = run(
        [
            binary,
            "bench",
            model,
            "--json",
            "--prompt",
            str(prompt),
            "-r",
            str(repetitions),
        ]
    )
    if out.returncode:
        return None
    return json.loads(out.stdout)


def llama(binary, model, prompt, generate, repetitions):
    out = run(
        [
            binary,
            "-m",
            model,
            "-p",
            str(prompt),
            "-n",
            str(generate),
            "-r",
            str(repetitions),
        ]
    )
    if out.returncode:
        return None
    row = {}
    for line in out.stdout.splitlines():
        cells = [c.strip() for c in line.strip().strip("|").split("|")]
        if len(cells) >= 7 and cells[-2] in (f"pp{prompt}", f"tg{generate}"):
            # "4262.90 ± 33.35": the mean comes first.
            row[cells[-2]] = float(re.match(r"[0-9.]+", cells[-1]).group())
    return row.get(f"pp{prompt}"), row.get(f"tg{generate}")


def main():
    assert agreed == 0 and diff[4] == "bc"
    assert compare(["a"], [{"token": "a"}, {"token": ""}], 0.1) == (2, None)


def main():
    self_check()
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("model")
    ap.add_argument("--kinetic", default="kinetic")
    ap.add_argument("--llama", required=True, help="folder with llama-server")
    ap.add_argument("--device", choices=["cpu", "cuda"], default="cpu")
    ap.add_argument("-n", type=int, default=64, help="tokens per prompt")
    ap.add_argument("--port", type=int, default=18080)
    ap.add_argument("--llama-arg", action="append", default=[],
                    help="extra llama-server argument, e.g. --llama-arg=-ncmoe --llama-arg=12")
    ap.add_argument("--tie", type=float, default=0.1, help="near-tie gap in nats")
    ap.add_argument("--early", type=int, default=16)
    a = ap.parse_args()

    texts = kinetic_texts(a)
    runs = llama_runs(a)
    print(f"{os.path.basename(a.model)} on {a.device}, {a.n} greedy tokens per prompt")
    failed = False
    total = agreed_all = 0
    for k, ((text, tokens), steps) in enumerate(zip(texts, runs)):
        if "".join(tokens) != text:
            print(f"prompt {k + 1}: kinetic text changes with logprobs")
            failed = True
            continue
        agreed, diff = compare(tokens, steps, a.tie)
        total += len(steps)
        agreed_all += agreed
        line = f"prompt {k + 1}: {agreed}/{len(steps)} tokens agree"
        if diff:
            pos, top, gap, tied, kin = diff
            alts = ", ".join(f"{t!r} {lp:.3f}" for t, lp in top)
            kind = "near-tie" if tied else "DIVERGES"
            gap = f"{gap:.3f}" if gap is not None else "?"
            line += f"; {kind} at token {pos}: llama.cpp top two {alts} (gap {gap}), kinetic {kin!r}"
            failed |= not tied and pos < a.early
        print(line)

Commandes de mesure communes\n\n### 5.1 Build et tests\n\n```sh\ncargo build --release --locked -p kinetic-cli --features vulkan\ncargo test --release --locked --workspace\ncargo test --release --locked -p kinetic-vulkan\ncargo test --release --locked -p kinetic-models\ncargo clippy --release --locked --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings\n```\n\n### 5.2 Inventaire\n\n```sh\ntarget/release/kinetic doctor\ntarget/release/kinetic info MODEL.gguf\n```\n\n### 5.3 Bench Vulkan\n\n```sh\ntarget/release/kinetic bench MODEL.gguf --device vulkan --json -r 6\nllama-bench -m MODEL.gguf -dev Vulkan0 -p 512 -n 128 -r 6\n```\n\n`kinetic bench` mesure `pp512`, `tg128` et `edit256`. Pour un préfill plus\nlong, utiliser `--prompt 2048`. Les chiffres se comparent toujours sur le\nmême fichier, le même backend et le même état machine.\n\n### 5.4 Protocole et conformance\n\n```sh\npython scripts/bench_protocol.py MODEL.gguf --llama-bin /path/to/llama-bench\npython scripts/conformance.py MODEL.gguf --kinetic target/release/kinetic \\\n  --llama /path/to/llama.cpp/bin --device cpu\n```\n\n`conformance.py` ne connaît aujourd'hui que `cpu` et `cuda`. L'extension à\n`vulkan` est un livrable QA. En attendant, lancer `kinetic serve --device\nvulkan` et comparer les tokens manuellement avec `llama-server`.\n\n### 5.5 Serveur\n\n```sh\npython scripts/llama_server_compat.py --model MODEL.gguf \\\n  --llama-server /path/to/llama-server --kinetic target/release/kinetic\npython scripts/server_abuse.py -- target/release/kinetic serve MODEL.gguf -c 512 --port 8091\npython scripts/same_answer_demo.py --model MODEL.gguf \\\n  --kinetic target/release/kinetic --kinetic-args \"--device vulkan\"\n```\n\n### 5.6 Vision\n\n```sh\ncargo run --release -p kinetic-vision --example encode -- mmproj.gguf rainbow:512\nllama-mtmd-debug --image rainbow -n 512 -m mmproj.gguf\n```\n\n### 5.7 Précautions\n\n- Un seul job GPU à la fois ; vérifier la machine idle (`rocm-smi`,\n  `radeontop`, aucun processus `kinetic`/`llama`).\n- Médiane de ≥ 6 échantillons ; contrôles avant et après chaque candidat.\n- Accepter seulement si le candidat bat les deux contrôles sur sa métrique et\n  ne régresse rien de plus de ~3 %.\n- Consigner chaque essai dans `PLAN.md` avec commande, commit, date, état\n  machine et verdict.\n- Ne jamais forcer un serveur en pleine passe : annuler les requêtes, laisser\n  drainer, puis arrêter avec un timeout.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Ce qu'il ne faut pas faire\n\n- **Ne pas recruter un « expert LLM » générique en premier.** Le goulot est\n  GPU/runtime, pas la théorie des transformers.\n- **Ne pas commencer par HIP.** Le décodage Vulkan est déjà à 95 % ; le\n  préfill est à 23 %. Le GEMM Vulkan est le meilleur premier chantier.\n- **Ne pas recruter un expert CUDA-only pour ce fork.** La machine n'a pas de\n  GPU NVIDIA ; il ne pourrait rien mesurer. CUDA est utile en amont/CI, pas\n  en P0 local.\n- **Ne pas lancer un chantier multimodal ou bindings avant la performance.**\n  C'est XL et hors chemin critique.\n- **Ne pas introduire un compilateur de graphes généraliste.** Une couche de\n  dispatch/exécution minimale suffit.\n- **Ne pas casser la culture d'exactitude.** Un gain non prouvé, ou qui change\n  la sortie, doit être rejeté.\n\n---\n\n## 7. Documents associés\n\n- [`docs/experts/fiches-de-poste.md`](experts/fiches-de-poste.md) : fiches de\n  poste détaillées pour les 10 profils.\n- [`docs/experts/prompts-agents.md`](experts/prompts-agents.md) : prompts\n  d'agents spécialisés, avec périmètre d'écriture, fichiers de contexte,\n  commandes de mesure et garde-fous.\n\n---\n\n## 8. Si quatre :\najouter **numérique**.\n\nLe reste — architectures, tokenizers, serveur, multimodal, bindings — peut\nêtre parallélisé, communautarisé ou recruté ensuite. Le projet a déjà les bons\nseams (`Family`, `Target`, `Backend`, `Projector`) et une documentation\nd'onboarding solide (`adding-a-family.md`, `contributing.md`) : un bon expert\ndoit pouvoir livrer une famille ou un noyau en quelques jours, pas en\nquelques semaines.\n"

d'inférence\n\n**Priorité** : P0 — chemin critique.\n**Rattachement** : équipe runtime/serveur.\n**Mission** : faire passer le serveur d'un modèle « N backends indépendants »\nà un ordonnanceur token-level qui tient la concurrence, le TTFT et le p99.\n\n### Contexte\n\n- `Engine.free` est un `Mutex<Vec<(usize, Box<dyn Backend>)>>` : une requête\n  par backend.\n- `PREFILL_CHUNK = 256` existe, mais le chunking est par requête.\n- `Convoy` mutualise des passes, mais ne planifie pas les requêtes.\n- Le KV est contigu par séquence, non paginé.\n- `MAX_CONNECTIONS = 64`, `Connection: close`, pas de keep-alive.\n- Les technologies RAD-1, Warm Start, Zero Wait, Shortlist et Convoy doivent\n  rester exactes.\n\n### Responsabilités\n\n- Concevoir un ordonnanceur token-level : admission, priorité, fairness,\n  annulation, backpressure.\n- Introduire un pool KV paginé, dimensionné pour N × contexte, avec\n  défragmentation et éviction.\n- Ajouter le chunked prefill global et le recouvrement préfill/décodage.\n- Gérer le rollback KV du spéculatif et la réutilisation de préfixe.\n- Intégrer le placement mémoire (layers, experts, tenseurs) et le multi-GPU.\n- Ajouter les métriques par token : TTFT, tok/s, p50/p99, cache hit, queue\n  depth.\n- Préserver les invariants d'exactitude et les tests existants.\n\n### Compétences requises\n\n- Continuous batching, paged KV, prefix caching, chunked prefill, admission\n  control, fairness, priorité, annulation, backpressure.\n- Décodage spéculatif : draft/verify, arbre, rollback, réutilisation de KV.\n- Rust concurrence : threads/async, `Mutex`/`Condvar`, channels, atomics,\n  `Send`/`Sync`, scoped threads, panic safety.\n- Mémoire : pool KV, fragmentation, mémoire unifiée, pinned host, paging des\n  experts, watchdog OOM.\n- Graph capture/replay, multi-stream.\n- Observabilité et mesure de latence.\n\n### Compétences appréciées\n\n- Expérience vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, llama.cpp server, ONNX Runtime.\n- Connaissance des modèles hybrides SSM/GDN et des slots d'état.\n- Expérience des systèmes locaux-first (pas cloud).\n\n### Périmètre d'écriture\n\n- `crates/kinetic-runtime/**` (à créer : ordonnanceur, pool KV, métriques)\n- `crates/kinetic-server/src/{engine,sequence,backend,server}.rs`\n- `crates/kinetic-models/src/{convoy,memory,per_layer}.rs`\n- `crates/kinetic-models/src/warm/**`\n- `PLAN.md`, `ledger.jsonl`, `configs/`\n\n### Fichiers de contexte\n\n- `PLAN.md` §4 P1.5 et P1.6.\n- `llama-kinetic.md` §7.6, §7.9, §7.10.\n- `crates/kinetic-server/src/engine.rs`, `sequence.rs`, `backend.rs`.\n- `crates/kinetic-models/src/convoy.rs`, `memory.rs`, `per_layer.rs`.\n- `crates/kinetic-models/src/warm/**`.\n- `docs/src/how-it-is-fast.md` (RAD-1, Warm Start, Zero Wait, Convoy).\n- `docs/src/devices.md` (layer split, MoE offload).\n\n### Commandes de mesure\n\n```sh\n# Serveur\ntarget/release/kinetic serve MODEL.gguf --device vulkan --parallel 4\n\n# Charge concurrente (exemple avec oha, ou un script maison)\noha -n 64 -c 4 --json http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions ...\n\n# Exactitude sous charge\npython scripts/same_answer_demo.py --model MODEL.gguf \\\n  --kinetic target/release/kinetic --kinetic-args \"--device vulkan\"\n\n# Robustesse\npython scripts/server_abuse.py --port 8091\n```\n\n### Livrables 30/60/90\n\n- **30 jours** : cartographie du runtime actuel, design doc, métriques\n  manquantes, prototype d'ordonnanceur.\n- **60 jours** : pool KV N × contexte, chunked prefill global, annulation,\n  métriques par token.\n- **90 jours** : benchmarks c1/c4/c16/c64, p99 et TTFT documentés, aucune\n  régression d'exactitude.\n\n### Critères de succès\n\n- Débit agrégé en hausse à c4/c16/c64.\n- p99 et TTFT mesurés et reproductibles.\n- `same_answer_demo.py` identique sous charge.\n- Aucun test d'identité cassé.\n- Aucune fuite mémoire ni cache non borné.\n\n### l'annulation.\n- Ne mesure que le débit moyen, jamais le p99.\n\n---\n\n## Fiche 3 — Architecte Rust systèmes/backend\n\n**Priorité** : P0/P1 — fondation.\n**Rattachement** : équipe cœur.\n**Mission** Les autres backend est pour le compatibilité mais effectivement, l'utilisateur n'en utilisera qu'un seul au final par rapport à sa carte et nous devons lui fournir les bases."

Interpretation: The user accepts the offer to transform analysis into docs/job descriptions/agent prompts, and also comments on the backend duplication: logically there should be one backend for CUDA and one for Vulkan, each containing all functionality. Other backends are compatibility; the user will only use one based on their card, and we must provide the bases.

The assistant already wrote docs incorporating this. The task now is likely to finish the response. But the user might expect actual refactor? "ne devrait avoir qu'un seul backend" is a design directive. The docs propose a migration. Should we implement the refactor? That's a huge task (~13k LOC moves) and not explicitly requested as code. The user said "j'accepte cela" referring to docs/job descriptions/agent prompts. So docs are the deliverable. We should not undertake a massive refactor unasked.

However, we might improve the docs with a concrete, actionable "backend consolidation" plan, perhaps a dedicated ADR/architecture doc, because the current section 0 is high-level. The user emphasized this point, so it deserves a clear, precise treatment:
- Define what "one backend" means: one crate per API containing driver, kernels, memory, graph, executor, capabilities.
- `kinetic-models` should be backend-agnostic; but there's a tension: model execution logic (layer orchestration) may be backend-specific because kernels differ. The current `kinetic-models/src/cuda` and `vulkan` are executors. Moving them into backend crates is sensible, but then `kinetic-models` needs a trait abstraction. The trait `Backend` is currently in `kinetic-server`, coarse (one request per backend). We need a lower-level `Executor` trait. The docs mention `kinetic-runtime` with `Backend`, `Device`, `Graph`, `Kernel`, `Capabilities`, `Memory`. But designing a generic graph/kernel abstraction across CUDA/Vulkan is nontrivial and could become a mini-compiler. The docs say no MLIR. Need to be careful: a trait at the model-execution level (e.g., `ModelExecutor` that takes tokens and returns logits) is simpler than a kernel-level abstraction. The user wants one backend per API, not necessarily a unified kernel IR.

Maybe the right architecture:
- `kinetic-runtime`: traits for `Executor` (model-level), `KvCache`, `DeviceInfo`, `Capabilities`, `BackendFactory`; not a kernel IR.

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct LoadError(pub String);

impl fmt::Display for LoadError {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(&self.0)
    }
}

impl std::error::Error for LoadError {}

/// Architectures Kinetic can run, by their GGUF name.
pub fn architectures() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static str> {
    arch::FAMILIES.iter().flat_map(|f| f.names.iter().copied())
}

/// Whether Kinetic runs the GGUF architecture `arch`.
pub fn supports(arch: &str) -> bool {
    arch::family(arch).is_some()
}

/// Whether `arch` is a BERT-style encoder, which only embeds.
pub fn is_encoder(arch: &str) -> bool {
    arch::family(arch).is_some_and(|f| matches!(f.body, Body::Encoder(_)))
}

/// Builds the model stored in `file`.
pub fn load(file: &dyn TensorSource) -> Result<Model<'_>, LoadError> {
    load_with(file, &RopeScaling::default())
}

/// [`load`] with the rotary scaling `rope` overriding the file's.
pub fn load_with<'a>(
    file: &'a dyn TensorSource,
    rope: &RopeScaling,
) -> Result<Model<'a>, LoadError> {
    let arch = architecture(file)?;
    if arch::family(arch).is_some_and(|f| !matches!(f.body, Body::Decoder(_))) {
        return Err(LoadError(format!(
            "{arch} is an encoder; load it with Embedder"
        )));
    }
    build(file, rope)
}

fn architecture(file: &dyn TensorSource) -> Result<&str, LoadError> {
    file.header()
        .architecture()
        .ok_or_else(|| LoadError("file does not name its architecture".into()))
}

    file: &'a dyn TensorSource,
    rope: &RopeScaling,
) -> Result<Model<'a>, LoadError> {

//! The seam between text handling and whatever runs the model.

use std::time::Duration;

use kinetic_grammar::{Grammar, Vocabulary};
use kinetic_models::Input;
use kinetic_vision::Embeddings;

use crate::{Logprobs, Sampling};

/// One generation request, in tokens.
pub struct Job<'j> {
    pub sampling: &'j Sampling,
    /// Most tokens to generate.
    pub max_tokens: usize,
    /// Generation ends after any of these.
    pub stop_tokens: &'j [u32],
    /// Output must match this grammar over this vocabulary.
    pub grammar: Option<(&'j Grammar, &'j Vocabulary)>,
    /// Images in the prompt, in order.
    pub images: &'j [PromptImage],
    /// Records the log-probability of every chosen token.
    pub logprobs: Option<&'j Logprobs>,
}

/// An encoded image whose rows take the place of the prompt's placeholder
/// tokens from `at` on, one token per row.
pub struct PromptImage {
    pub at: usize,
    pub image: Embeddings,
}

/// The entries of `prompt` up to its last token, which must be text, with
/// image rows in place of their placeholder tokens.
pub fn image_inputs<'p>(prompt: &'p [u32], images: &'p [PromptImage]) -> Vec<Input<'p>> {
    let mut inputs = Vec::with_capacity(2 * images.len() + 1);
    let mut at = 0;
    for p in images {
        inputs.push(Input::Tokens(&prompt[at..p.at]));
        inputs.push(Input::Image {
            rows: &p.image.rows,
            width: p.image.width,
            height: p.image.height,
        });
        at = p.at + p.image.len();
    }
    inputs.push(Input::Tokens(&prompt[at..prompt.len() - 1]));
    inputs
}

/// Where the time of one generation went.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Timings {
    pub prompt_tokens: usize,
    /// Leading prompt tokens already in the cache from the previous request.
    pub cached_tokens: usize,
    pub prefill: Duration,
    pub generated: usize,
    pub decode: Duration,
}

/// Runs a model on some device. Implementations keep whatever per-sequence
/// state they like between calls, such as the cache of the last prompt.
pub trait Backend: Send {
    /// Runs `prompt` and generates after it, handing each batch of new tokens
    /// to `emit`. Stops after a stop token, after `max_tokens`, or when
    /// `emit` returns false.
    fn generate(
        &mut self,
        prompt: &[u32],
        job: &Job,
        emit: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u32]) -> bool,
    ) -> Timings;

    /// How many leading tokens of `prompt` this backend has run already and
    /// would not run again. Of several free backends, a request goes to
    /// the one that reuses the most.
    fn reuses(&self, _prompt: &[u32]) -> usize {
        0
    }

    /// Runs the next batch of `prompt` that a request for it, or for any
    /// longer prompt starting with it, would run first, so that request
    /// starts further in and generates exactly what it would have; returns
    /// how many leading tokens of `prompt` are run. The same count again
    /// means nothing is left to run ahead.
    fn run_ahead(&mut self, _prompt: &[u32]) -> usize {
        0
    }

    /// Whether the last request left work that the next one to continue
    /// its sequence would otherwise run first; see [`Backend::settle_some`].
    fn unsettled(&self) -> bool {
        false
    }

    /// Runs a short piece of the work [`Backend::unsettled`] tells of, so
    /// that a request that comes while the backend is idle need not wait
    /// for it all. What a request generates is the same either way.
    fn settle_some(&mut self) {}
}

use std::sync::{Arc, OnceLock};

use kinetic_cpu::{matmul, pool, rms_norm};
use kinetic_quant::{dequantize_row, Matrix};

use crate::blocks::{end_lending, lend_kv, Folding, Mixer, MixerState, Moe, Part, SwiGlu, Tree};
use crate::convoy::{Convoy, Seat};
use crate::head::Shortlist;
use crate::per_layer::PerLayer;

/// One decoder layer: a token mixer and a feed-forward network, each with
/// optional normalization of its input and output, an optional scale, and
/// a residual connection. In a mixture-of-experts layer the feed-forward
/// is the routed experts plus, if the model has one, a shared expert.
pub(crate) struct Layer<'a> {
    pub mixer_norm: Option<Vec<f32>>,
    pub mixer: Mixer<'a>,
    pub mixer_out_norm: Option<Vec<f32>>,
    pub ffn_norm: Option<Vec<f32>>,
    pub ffn: Option<SwiGlu<'a>>,
    pub experts: Option<Moe<'a>>,
    pub ffn_out_norm: Option<Vec<f32>>,
    /// Multiplies the mixer and feed-forward outputs before they join the
    /// residual stream.
    pub residual_scale: Option<f32>,
    /// Multiplies the stream once the layer is done.
    pub out_scale: Option<f32>,
}

impl Layer<'_> {
    /// The width of the hidden state.
    pub(crate) fn width(&self) -> usize {
        match (&self.ffn, &self.experts) {
            (Some(f), _) => f.down.rows,
            (None, Some(moe)) => moe.router.cols,
            (None, None) => unreachable!("a layer has a feed-forward"),
        }
    }

    /// Applies the layer to `x`, rows of hidden states, in place.
    pub(crate) fn forward(
        &self,
        x: &mut [f32],
        eps: f32,
        pos0: usize,
        grid: Option<&[[usize; 3]]>,
        tree: Option<&Tree>,
        state: &mut MixerState,
    ) {
        self.forward_with(x, eps, |h| self.mixer.forward(h, pos0, grid, tree, state));
    }

    /// [`Layer::forward`] on a batch made of `parts`, each on its own state.
    fn forward_parts(&self, x: &mut [f32], eps: f32, parts: &mut [Part]) {
        self.forward_with(x, eps, |h| self.mixer.forward_parts(h, parts));
    }

    /// [`Layer::forward`] with `mix` in place of the mixer.
    pub(crate) fn forward_with(
        &self,
        x: &mut [f32],
        eps: f32,
        mix: impl FnOnce(&[f32]) -> Vec<f32>,
    ) {
        let d = self.width();
        let norm = |x: &mut [f32], w: &Option<Vec<f32>>| {
            if let Some(w) = w {
                pool::for_each_chunk(x, d, |_, row| rms_norm(row, w, eps));
            }
        };
        let scale = self.residual_scale.unwrap_or(1.0);
        let add = |x: &mut [f32], y: &[f32]| {
            pool::for_each_chunk(x, d, |t, row| {
                row.iter_mut()
                    .zip(&y[t * d..])
                    .for_each(|(x, y)| *x += y * scale)
            })
        };
        let mut h = x.to_vec();
        norm(&mut h, &self.mixer_norm);
        let mut mixed = mix(&h);
        norm(&mut mixed, &self.mixer_out_norm);
        add(x, &mixed);

        h.copy_from_slice(x);
        norm(&mut h, &self.ffn_norm);
        let mut ffn = match &self.ffn {
            Some(f) => f.forward(&h),
            None => vec![0.0; h.len()],
        };
        if let Some(moe) = &self.experts {
            moe.forward(&h, &mut ffn);
        }
        norm(&mut ffn, &self.ffn_out_norm);
        add(x, &ffn);
        if let Some(out) = self.out_scale {
            pool::for_each_chunk(x, d, |_, row| row.iter_mut().for_each(|v| *v *= out));
        }
    }
}

//! Model families. Each file declares the [`Family`] it builds; [`FAMILIES`]
//! lists them all, and loading, support checks and listings read only that
//! list.

pub(crate) mod bert;
pub(crate) mod falcon_h1;
pub(crate) mod gemma4;
pub(crate) mod gemma_embedding;
pub(crate) mod granite;
pub(crate) mod lfm2;
pub(crate) mod lfm3;
mod mamba;
mod moe;
pub(crate) mod qwen35;
pub(crate) mod rope;
pub(crate) mod transformer;

use crate::arch::bert::Encoder;
use crate::folds::Folds;
use crate::loader::Loader;
use crate::model::{Layer, Mtp};
use crate::per_layer::PerLayer;
use crate::LoadError;

/// Every family Kinetic runs.
pub(crate) const FAMILIES: &[Family] = &[
    qwen35::FAMILY,
    lfm3::FAMILY,
    lfm2::FAMILY,
    transformer::FAMILY,
    transformer::GEMMA3,
    gemma4::FAMILY,
    granite::FAMILY,
    falcon_h1::FAMILY,
    bert::FAMILY,
    transformer::GEMMA_EMBEDDING,
];

/// The family whose GGUF architecture name is `arch`.
pub(crate) fn family(arch: &str) -> Option<&'static Family> {
    FAMILIES.iter().find(|f| f.names.contains(&arch))
}

/// One model family: the GGUF architecture names it answers to, how its
/// layers are built and the few ways its embedding and head differ.
#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) struct Family {
    pub names: &'static [&'static str],
    pub body: Body,
    /// Tensor holding the weights of the norm before the output head.
    pub output_norm: &'static str,
    /// Embeddings are scaled by the square root of the width, as in Gemma.
    pub sqrt_embd_scale: bool,
    /// Logits are divided by the file's `logit_scale`, as in Granite.
    pub logit_scale: bool,
}

impl Family {
    /// A text decoder with the usual embedding and head.
    pub const fn decoder(names: &'static [&'static str], layers: BuildLayers) -> Family {
        Family {
            names,
            body: Body::Decoder(layers),
            output_norm: "output_norm.weight",
            sqrt_embd_scale: false,
            logit_scale: false,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
pub(crate) enum Body {
    /// Generates text.
    Decoder(BuildLayers),
    /// Decoder layers in which every token sees the whole input, for
    /// embeddings only.
    Bidirectional(BuildLayers),
    /// A BERT-style encoder with its own loader, for embeddings only.
    Encoder(BuildEncoder),
}

pub(crate) type BuildLayers = for<'a> fn(&Loader<'a>, &Basics) -> Result<Stack<'a>, LoadError>;
pub(crate) type BuildEncoder = for<'a> fn(&Loader<'a>, &str) -> Result<Encoder<'a>, LoadError>;

/// What every layer builder gets besides the file.
pub(crate) struct Basics<'f> {
    /// The file's architecture name, for families that answer to several.
    pub arch: &'f str,
    pub d: usize,
    pub eps: f32,
    pub folds: Option<&'f Folds>,
}

/// The layers a builder returns, the prediction block if the file has one
/// and the per-layer token inputs if the model has them.
pub(crate) struct Stack<'a> {
    pub layers: Vec<Layer<'a>>,
    pub mtp: Option<Mtp<'a>>,
    pub per_layer: Option<PerLayer<'a>>,
}

_Thinking:_

The architecture: `kinetic-models` contains generic CPU model execution plus optional CUDA/Vulkan executors. `kinetic-server` has `cpu.rs`, `cuda.rs`, `vulkan.rs` implementing `Backend` by wrapping model executors. So "one backend per API" means:
- `kinetic-cuda` should contain `kinetic-models/src/cuda` executor code.
- `kinetic-vulkan` should contain `kinetic-models/src/vulkan`.
- `kinetic-models` stays generic (architectures/blocks) and CPU execution.
- `kinetic-server` should not have per-backend modules; a factory picks the backend.

But if `kinetic-models` is generic over CPU and GPU, the CUDA/Vulkan executors need access to `Model` internals (pub(crate)). Moving them into separate crates would require exposing internals or moving the model orchestration too. That's a significant design challenge. The docs propose `kinetic-runtime` traits. We should be precise about what moves and what stays. The current `kinetic-models/src/cuda` and `vulkan` are model executors that use `kinetic-models` internals (`Model`, `Layer`, etc.) and are part of the same crate. Moving them out requires public APIs or a trait. The doc's migration step "Déplacer kinetic-models/src/cuda vers kinetic-cuda/src/executor" is not purely mechanical; it requires exposing model structures or defining an executor trait. The docs say "déplacement mécanique" which may be misleading. We should adjust: "déplacement mécanique après extraction d'une interface de modèle (ou via un module `pub` contrôlé)" and note the risk.

This is important: the user wants a credible architecture. We shouldn't claim a mechanical move when it isn't. Let's think about the best target architecture.

Option A: Model-level backend trait
- `kinetic-models` defines `trait ModelBackend` / `Executor` with methods like `load`, `forward`, `generate`, `state`, etc. Each GPU crate implements it. But each GPU executor needs to know architecture details (layers, blocks). It can use `kinetic-models` public descriptors. //! Generation on a Vulkan GPU.

use std::cell::Cell;
use std::time::Instant;

use kinetic_models::speculative::{Decoder, Ensemble, Policy};
use kinetic_models::vulkan::{VulkanModel, VulkanRunner, VulkanState};
use kinetic_models::warm::Warm;
use kinetic_models::{LoadError, Model, State};

use crate::backend::{Backend, Job, Timings};
use crate::cpu::CpuBackend;
use crate::drafter::{self, Source};
use crate::sequence::{self, Run, Sequence, PREFILL_CHUNK};

/// Runs a model on a Vulkan GPU (AMD, Intel or NVIDIA) with the guarantees
/// of [`CpuBackend`]: speculative decoding that changes no token, greedy or
/// seeded, reuse of the last sequence when a prompt extends it and, with a
/// [`Warm`] cache, warm starts that give exactly the output of a cold run.
/// Prompts with images run on the CPU, since the device takes only token
/// ids.
pub struct VulkanBackend<'a> {
    gpu: VulkanModel<'a>,
    model: &'a Model<'a>,
    decoder: Decoder<Ensemble<Source<VulkanModel<'a>>>>,
    cached: Option<Sequence<VulkanState>>,
    warm: Option<Warm<'a>>,
    cpu: CpuBackend<'a>,
    device: String,
}

/// A prompt's state to keep in the warm cache once the reply is out.
struct Keep {
    tokens: Vec<u32>,
    state: State,
    logits: Vec<f32>,
}

// SAFETY: `VulkanModel` and the states made from it are not `Send` only
// because they share their device through `Rc`. Every one of those
// resources, and so every `Rc` to the device, is owned by this backend and
// never handed out, so they all move between threads together; `Backend`
// takes `&mut self`, so one thread drives the device at a time.
unsafe impl Send for VulkanBackend<'_> {}

fn vulkan_error(e: kinetic_vulkan::Error) -> LoadError {
    LoadError(format!("Vulkan: {e}"))
}

impl<'a> VulkanBackend<'a> {
    /// Uploads `model` to the first Vulkan device that can run it, for
    /// sequences of up to `context` tokens. Fails when no device is usable
    /// or the model needs something the Vulkan kernels lack.
    pub fn new(model: &'a Model<'a>, context: usize) -> Result<Self, LoadError> {
        let gpu = VulkanModel::load(model, context)?;
        let state = gpu.new_state().map_err(vulkan_error)?;
        // the drafter's cache shares the memory, so a full device fails here
        // and not on the first request
        drop(gpu.new_mtp_state().map_err(vulkan_error)?);
        Ok(VulkanBackend {
            decoder: drafter::decoder(&gpu),
            cached: Some(Sequence {
                state,
                tokens: Vec::new(),
            }),
            warm: None,
            cpu: CpuBackend::new(model),
            device: format!("{} ({})", gpu.device_name(), kinetic_vulkan::API),
            model,
            gpu,
        })
    }

    /// [`VulkanBackend::new`] that never drafts, so every token costs one
    /// forward pass, as benchmarks want.
    pub fn plain(model: &'a Model<'a>, context: usize) -> Result<Self, LoadError> {
        VulkanBackend::new(model, context).map(Self::without_drafts)
    }

    /// Turns RAD-1 off: every token costs one forward pass.
    pub fn without_drafts(mut self) -> Self {
        self.decoder.max_draft = 0;
        VulkanBackend {
            cpu: self.cpu.without_drafts(),
            ..self
        }
    }

    /// Starts every new sequence from the longest prefix `warm` holds, and
    /// keeps each new prompt's state there. `warm` must hold only states
    /// this device made; see [`kinetic_models::warm::device_id`].
    pub fn with_warm(mut self, warm: Warm<'a>) -> Self {
        self.warm = Some(warm.aligned(PREFILL_CHUNK));
        self
    }

    /// The name of the device the model runs on, marked as run through
    /// Vulkan.
    pub fn device(&self) -> &str {
        &self.device
    }

    /// The cached sequence when `prompt` extends it, else a new one, run up
    /// to the end of `prompt` with the token after it chosen; the number of
    /// tokens reused; and the state to keep warm, if any.
    fn prefill(
        &mut self,

                    &self.gpu,
                    &mut self.decoder,
                    policy,
                    &mut seq,

                    chunk,
                );
                return (seq, reused, None);

//! Whole models on a Vulkan GPU: AMD, Intel or NVIDIA.
//!
//! [`VulkanModel::load`] uploads the weights of a loaded [`Model`] once; a
//! [`VulkanState`] holds a sequence's caches and working buffers on the
//! device. Token embeddings and rotary angles are computed on the host,
//! exactly as the CPU path computes them; greedy tokens, hidden states and,
//! when asked for, logits come back.
//!
//! A state records its pass once, as a command buffer replayed for every
//! batch of up to [`MAX_BATCH`] tokens: the kernels read how many tokens run
//! and where from a small buffer the host fills before each run. Every
//! kernel computes a token's result the same way whatever else shares its
//! batch, so a verified speculative draft yields exactly the tokens plain
//! decoding would. Attention caches and convolution rings are indexed by
//! position, so a rollback has nothing to undo there; delta-rule layers
//! leave their state alone after a checkpoint and replay the kept tokens
//! from a journal on rollback.

/// Most tokens one pass runs, prompt passes apart, and most that may run
/// between a checkpoint and its rollback.
pub const MAX_BATCH: usize = 16;

/// Fewest tokens worth a prompt pass: below, the kernels a token is
/// decoded with are the faster ones.
const PROMPT_MIN: usize = 4;

/// Most tokens a prompt pass runs: what the driver asks for, or
/// [`MAX_BATCH`] if it has no kernels of its own for such passes. They
/// give every token the bits it gets alone, so nothing but speed depends
/// on how a prompt is split.
const PROMPT_BATCH: usize = larger(kinetic_vulkan::PROMPT_BATCH, MAX_BATCH);

// Not `max`: clippy refuses to compare the 0 of a driver without a prompt
// kernel as a constant.
const fn larger(a: usize, b: usize) -> usize {
    if a > b {
        a
    } else {
        b
    }
}

/// The device and its kernels.
struct Gpu {
    device: Rc<Device>,
    kernels: Kernels,
}

impl Gpu {
    fn matrix(&self, m: &Matrix) -> Result<DeviceMatrix, LoadError> {
        DeviceMatrix::upload(&self.device, m).map_err(vulkan_error)
    }

    fn vector(&self, v: &[f32]) -> Result<DeviceBuffer<f32>, LoadError> {
        DeviceBuffer::from_slice(&self.device, v).map_err(vulkan_error)
    }
}

fn vulkan_error(e: kinetic_vulkan::Error) -> LoadError {
    match e {
        kinetic_vulkan::Error::Unsupported(ty) => {
            let api = kinetic_vulkan::API;
            LoadError(format!(
                "{api} has no kernel for {ty}, a weight type this model uses; it runs on \
                 the CPU (--device cpu), and K-quants such as Q4_K_M have {api} kernels"
            ))
        }
        e => LoadError(format!("Vulkan: {e}")),
    }
}

/// The Vulkan devices that can run models, discrete GPUs first.
pub fn devices() -> kinetic_vulkan::Result<Vec<PhysicalDevice>> {
    let mut devices = Instance::new()?.physical_devices()?;
    devices.retain(|d| d.info().missing().is_none());
    Ok(devices)
}

```
> ses noyaux dans `kinetic-cpu`, son exécution générique dans `kinetic-models`.
> `kinetic-models` ne contient plus de code CUDA/Vulkan : il décrit les
> architectures, les blocs et les invariants, et expose une interface
> d'exécution **au niveau modèle** (charger, préfill, décoder, état de
> séquence, capacités), pas au niveau noyau.

Les autres API (HIP, Metal, SYCL, WebGPU) sont des **backends de
compatibilité** : chacun est complet pour son API, mais n'est ajouté que
lorsqu'une machine et une CI peuvent le valider. L'utilisateur n'en charge
qu'un seul à l'exécution, selon sa carte. On fournit le socle (trait,
capacités, tests de conformance, modèle de build), pas une implémentation
complète et invérifiable de chaque API.

### 0.1 État actuel vs cible

| Aujourd'hui | Cible |
|---|---|
| CUDA : `kinetic-cuda` + `kinetic-models/src/cuda` | `kinetic-cuda` contient tout CUDA |
| Vulkan : `kinetic-vulkan` + `kinetic-models/src/vulkan` | `kinetic-vulkan` contient tout Vulkan |
| `kinetic-models` a des features `cuda` / `vulkan` et des modules backend | `kinetic-models` sans feature backend, expose un trait `Runner` |
| `kinetic-server` a `cuda.rs`, `vulkan.rs`, `cpu.rs` | `kinetic-server` choisit un backend via une factory |
| Ajouter HIP = nouveau crate + nouveau module dans `kinetic-models` | Ajouter HIP = nouveau crate qui implémente `Runner` |
| Les tests modèle connaissent les backends | Les tests modèle utilisent le runner CPU ou un mock |

### 0.2 Où vivent les traits

Deux couches, pas une :

- **`kinetic-runtime`** (à créer) : découverte des devices, registre/factory
  de backends, capacités, budget mémoire, ordonnanceur, pool KV, métriques.
  Il ne connaît **pas** les types de modèle.
- **`kinetic-models`** : architectures, blocs, modèle générique, trait
  `Runner` au niveau modèle, runner CPU de référence.
- **`kinetic-cuda` / `kinetic-vulkan` / `kinetic-hip`** : implémentent
  `Runner` et possèdent leurs noyaux, graphes et politiques de mémoire.

Cette séparation évite un cycle de dépendances et évite de transformer
`kinetic-runtime` en compilateur de graphes. Le trait `Runner` reste petit :
charger, préfill, décoder, état de séquence, capacités. Chaque backend garde
la liberté de fusionner, grapher et ordonnancer ses noyaux comme il veut.

### 0.3 Migration incrémentale

1. Créer `kinetic-runtime` avec les types de devices, capacités, budget
   mémoire et factory. Aucun changement de comportement.
2. Extraire dans `kinetic-models` un trait `Runner` au niveau modèle et
   exposer les descripteurs nécessaires aux backends. Le runner CPU existant
   devient l'implémentation de référence.
3. Déplacer `kinetic-models/src/cuda` vers `kinetic-cuda/src/runner` et
   `kinetic-models/src/vulkan` vers `kinetic-vulkan/src/runner`. Ce n'est pas
   un simple `git mv` : il faut passer par le trait et les descripteurs
   exposés, et conserver les tests à chaque étape.
4. Retirer les features `cuda` / `vulkan` de `kinetic-models` ; il ne dépend
   plus des crates backend.
5. Ajouter une factory de backend dans `kinetic-server` / `kinetic-cli` :
   `auto | cpu | cuda | vulkan | hip`, un seul backend chargé.
6. Ajouter un backend de test (CPU ou mock) pour tester `kinetic-models`
   sans GPU.
7. Seulement ensuite, optimiser. Le refactor d'abord ; la performance vient
   après, avec les mêmes gates d'exactitude.

### 0.4 Contrat de compatibilité d'un backend

Un backend n'est « fourni » que s'il respecte ce contrat :

- **Découverte** : `probe()` liste les devices et leurs capacités réelles.
- **Capacités** : types de poids, formats KV, batch max, async, multi-device,
  mémoire disponible. Le serveur refuse clairement ce qui n'est pas supporté.
- **Conformance** : mêmes tokens que le runner CPU sur le corpus de contrôle,
  aux tolérances près, et mêmes gates d'identité.
- **Mesure** : `kinetic bench` et le protocole A/B fonctionnent sur ce
  backend, avec un seuil de régression.
- **Isolement** : un seul backend est chargé à l'exécution ; les autres ne
  coûtent ni mémoire ni temps de démarrage.
- **CI** : au moins un runner ou une machine de référence valide le backend
  avant qu'il ne soit activé par défaut.

Tant qu'un backend ne passe pas ce contrat, il reste **opt-in** et documenté
comme expérimental. C'est ainsi qu'on fournit les bases de HIP/Metal/SYCL
sans promettre une parité invérifiable.
```

//! Warm starts: prompts that begin like an earlier one resume from that
//! one's exact state and run only their new tokens.
//!
//! Agents and chat clients resend the same system prompt, tools and history
//! with every request. [`Warm`] keeps the states those prompts left behind,
//! in memory under a byte budget and optionally on disk, and starts each
//! new prompt from the longest cached prefix it can return to exactly.
//! Attention caches cut back to any length; recurrent layers only to the
//! marks taken every few hundred tokens, where prompts part and where they
//! resume.
//!
//! A restored state is bit for bit the one its run left behind, so a warm
//! prefill gives exactly the logits of a cold one on models whose results
//! do not depend on how a prompt is split into batches, as the speculative
//! decoder already requires of every block. Otherwise it matches a cold run
//! with the same batch boundaries, and a single batch up to rounding;
//! [`Warm::aligned`] makes those boundaries the same by construction.

mod codec;
mod disk;
mod hash;
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests;

use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{self, Read};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant, SystemTime};

use crate::{Model, State};
use disk::Disk;
use hash::Hasher;

/// Marks are taken at multiples of this many tokens, or of a larger
/// multiple of it when a mark is expensive next to the cache it saves.
const GRID: usize = 256;
const MAX_GRID: usize = 8192;

/// What runs prompts for a [`Warm`] cache: the [`Model`] itself, or a copy
/// of it on a device whose states have an exact host form.
pub trait Runner {
    /// A sequence's state where it runs.
    type State;
    /// The runner's copy of a host state.
    fn restore(&self, state: State) -> Self::State;
    /// Number of tokens `state` has run.
    fn len(&self, state: &Self::State) -> usize;
    /// Runs `tokens` and returns the logits after the last one.
    fn forward(&self, state: &mut Self::State, tokens: &[u32]) -> Vec<f32>;
    /// Saves what a later truncation needs to return to the current length,
    /// as [`Model::mark`] does.
    fn mark(&self, state: &mut Self::State);
    /// Seconds per byte of host state that [`Runner::restore`] is expected
    /// to take before any restore has been timed.
    fn restore_rate(&self) -> f64;
}

impl Runner for Model<'_> {
    type State = State;

    fn restore(&self, state: State) -> State {
        state
    }

    fn len(&self, state: &State) -> usize {
        state.len()
    }

    fn forward(&self, state: &mut State, tokens: &[u32]) -> Vec<f32> {
        self.forward_batch(state, tokens)
    }

    fn mark(&self, state: &mut State) {
        Model::mark(self, state);
    }

    fn restore_rate(&self) -> f64 {
        // A clone, at the speed of a memory copy.
        1.0 / 8e9
    }
}

/// What a prefill reused and what it cost.
pub struct Prefill<S = State> {
    /// The state after the whole prompt, ready to decode from.
    pub state: S,
    /// Logits after the last prompt token.
    pub logits: Vec<f32>,
    /// Prompt tokens restored from the cache rather than run.
    pub hit: usize,
    pub elapsed: Duration,
    /// Estimated time running the restored tokens would have taken, from
    /// the speed measured when they first ran.
    pub saved: Duration,
}

/// What an entry holds, without its state: enough to rank it for a prompt.
#[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
struct Meta {
    tokens: Vec<u32>,
    marks: Vec<usize>,
    /// Whether the state cuts back to any shorter length in place.
    in_place: bool,
    /// Seconds per token of the prefill that produced it.
    rate: f64,
}

Retirer les features `cuda` / `vulkan` de `kinetic-models` ; il ne dépend\n   plus des crates backend.\n5. Ajouter une factory de backend dans `kinetic-server` / `kinetic-cli` :\n   `auto | cpu | cuda | vulkan | hip`, un seul backend chargé.\n6. Ajouter un backend de test (CPU ou mock) pour tester `kinetic-models`\n   sans GPU.\n7. Seulement ensuite, optimiser. Le refactor d'abord ; la performance vient\n   après, avec les mêmes gates d'exactitude.\n\n### 0.4 Contrat de compatibilité d'un backend\n\nUn backend n'est « fourni » que s'il respecte ce contrat :\n\n- **Découverte** : `probe()` liste les devices et leurs capacités réelles.\n- **Capacités** : types de poids, formats KV, batch max, async, multi-device,\n  mémoire disponible. Le serveur refuse clairement ce qui n'est pas supporté.\n- **Conformance** : mêmes tokens que le runner CPU sur le corpus de contrôle,\n  aux tolérances près, et mêmes gates d'identité.\n- **Mesure** : `kinetic bench` et le protocole A/B fonctionnent sur ce\n  backend, avec un seuil de régression.\n- **Isolement** : un seul backend est chargé à l'exécution ; les autres ne\n  coûtent ni mémoire ni temps de démarrage.\n- **CI** : au moins un runner ou une machine de référence valide le backend\n  avant qu'il ne soit activé par défaut.\n\nTant qu'un backend ne passe pas ce contrat, il reste **opt-in** et documenté\ncomme expérimental. C'est ainsi qu'on fournit les bases de HIP/Metal/SYCL\nsans promettre une parité invérifiable.\n\n### 0.5 Ce que cela change pour les experts\n\n- **GPU AMD** travaille dans `kinetic-vulkan` et `kinetic-hip`, pas dans\n  `kinetic-models`.\n- **Runtime** travaille dans `kinetic-runtime` et `kinetic-server`, pas dans\n  les crates backend.\n- **Rust backend** pilote la migration et garde les seams `Family`,\n  `Target`, `Backend`, `Projector`.\n- **Quantification** travaille dans `kinetic-quant` et les noyaux, avec une\n  seule définition de référence.\n- **Intégration modèles** travaille dans `kinetic-models/src/arch` et\n  `blocks`, sans code backend.\n- **QA** teste chaque backend séparément avec le même corpus et les mêmes\n  gates.\n\n### 0.6 Non-objectifs\n\n- Pas de compilateur de graphes généraliste (MLIR ou équivalent).\n- Pas d'ABI de plugins dynamiques au départ : les features Cargo suffisent.\n- Pas de noyau « universel » qui serait lent partout : chaque backend\n  optimise son chemin.\n- Pas de backend CUDA prioritaire sur cette machine : pas de GPU NVIDIA,\n  donc pas de mesure locale."
```json
}
```

//! Generation on the CPU with `kinetic-models`.

use std::time::Instant;

use kinetic_models::speculative::{Decoder, Ensemble, Policy};
use kinetic_models::warm::Warm;
use kinetic_models::{Model, State};

use crate::backend::{image_inputs, Backend, Job, PromptImage, Timings};
use crate::drafter::{self, Source};
use crate::sequence::{self, Run, Sequence, PREFILL_CHUNK, PREFILL_GRID};

/// Runs a [`Model`] on the CPU with lossless speculative decoding: greedy
/// requests produce exactly the plain greedy tokens, and sampled ones draw
/// every token from exactly the distribution plain sampling would, the same
/// tokens for the same seed. The last sequence stays cached, so a prompt
/// that extends it, such as the next turn of a chat, only runs its new
/// tokens; with a [`Warm`] cache, any prompt resumes from the longest prefix
/// an earlier one left behind.
pub struct CpuBackend<'a> {
    model: &'a Model<'a>,
    decoder: Decoder<Ensemble<Source<Model<'a>>>>,
    cached: Option<Sequence<State>>,
    /// The length `cached` had when it began to run ahead of a request.
    ahead: Option<usize>,
    warm: Option<Warm<'a>>,
}

/// A prompt's state to keep in the warm cache once the reply is out.
struct Keep {
    tokens: Vec<u32>,
    state: State,
    logits: Vec<f32>,
}

impl<'a> CpuBackend<'a> {
    pub fn new(model: &'a Model<'a>) -> Self {
        model.page_in_experts();
        CpuBackend {
            model,
            decoder: drafter::decoder(model),
            cached: None,
            ahead: None,
            warm: None,
        }
    }

    /// A backend that never drafts, so every token costs one forward pass,
    /// as benchmarks want.
    pub fn plain(model: &'a Model<'a>) -> Self {
        CpuBackend::new(model).without_drafts()
    }

    /// Turns RAD-1 off: every token costs one forward pass.
    pub fn without_drafts(mut self) -> Self {
        self.decoder.max_draft = 0;
        self
    }

    /// Starts every new sequence from the longest prefix `warm` holds, and
    /// keeps each new prompt's state there. Warm starts resume where a cold
    /// prefill cuts its batches, so they give exactly its output.
    pub fn with_warm(mut self, warm: Warm<'a>) -> Self {
        self.warm = Some(warm.aligned(PREFILL_CHUNK));
        self
    }

    /// The cached sequence when `prompt` extends it, else a new one, run up
    /// to the end of `prompt` with the token after it chosen; the number of
    /// tokens reused; and the state to keep warm, if any.
    fn prefill(
        &mut self,
        prompt: &[u32],
        policy: &mut impl Policy<Model<'a>>,
    ) -> (Sequence<State>, usize, Option<Keep>) {
        self.rewind(prompt);
        if let Some(mut seq) = self.cached.take_if(|s| s.continues(prompt)) {
            let reused = seq.tokens.len();
            self.extend(&mut seq, prompt, policy);
            return (seq, reused, None);

//! The generation loop every backend shares: prefill a cached sequence,
//! then decode speculatively under a [`Policy`].

use kinetic_models::speculative::{Decoder, Drafter, Greedy, Policy, Sampler, Target};

use crate::backend::{Job, Timings};
use crate::constrained::Constrained;

/// Prompt tokens per forward pass on the CPU; bounds the activations of
/// long prompts. Prompts are cut at multiples of a backend's chunk, which is
/// also where its warm starts resume, so both run the same batches.
pub const PREFILL_CHUNK: usize = 256;

/// CPU prompt runs give the same bits wherever they are cut on multiples of
/// this many tokens after where they started: delta-net layers run batches
/// of 32 or more in chunks of 16, and fewer token by token.
pub const PREFILL_GRID: usize = 32;

/// A sequence a backend keeps between requests.
pub struct Sequence<S> {
    pub state: S,
    /// Every token `state` has run.
    pub tokens: Vec<u32>,
}

impl<S> Sequence<S> {
    /// Whether `prompt` continues this sequence with at least one new token.
    pub fn continues(&self, prompt: &[u32]) -> bool {
        prompt.len() > self.tokens.len() && prompt.starts_with(&self.tokens)
    }
}

/// A backend that runs a request under any policy; [`generate`] picks the
/// policy the request asks for.
pub trait Run<M: Target> {
    fn run<P: Policy<M>>(
        &mut self,
        prompt: &[u32],
        job: &Job,
        policy: &mut P,
        emit: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u32]) -> bool,
    ) -> Timings;
}

/// Runs `job` on `backend` with greedy choice, seeded sampling or a
/// grammar, as the job asks.
pub fn generate<M: Target, B: Run<M>>(
    backend: &mut B,
    prompt: &[u32],
    job: &Job,
    emit: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u32]) -> bool,
) -> Timings {
    assert!(!prompt.is_empty(), "empty prompt");
    let greedy = job.sampling.is_greedy() && job.logprobs.is_none();
    let sampler = || {
        let sampler = Sampler::new(job.sampling.clone());
        match job.logprobs {
            Some(log) => sampler.with_logprobs(log.clone()),
            None => sampler,
        }
    };
    if let Some((grammar, vocab)) = job.grammar {
        let mut policy = Constrained::new(grammar, vocab, prompt.len(), (!greedy).then(sampler));
        return backend.run(prompt, job, &mut policy, emit);
    }
    if greedy {
        backend.run(prompt, job, &mut Greedy, emit)
    } else {
        backend.run(prompt, job, &mut sampler(), emit)
    }
}

/// Runs the tokens of `prompt` that `seq` has not run in chunks of `chunk`,
/// the leading ones without choosing and the last through `policy`, which
/// chooses the token after the prompt.
pub fn extend<M: Target, P: Policy<M>, D: Drafter<M>>(
    model: &M,
    decoder: &mut Decoder<D>,
    policy: &mut P,
    seq: &mut Sequence<M::State>,
    prompt: &[u32],
    chunk: usize,
) {
    let start = seq.tokens.len();
    let last = start + (prompt.len() - start - 1) / chunk * chunk;
    for chunk in prompt[start..last].chunks(chunk) {
        decoder.feed(model, &mut seq.state, chunk);
    }
    seq.tokens.extend_from_slice(&prompt[start..]);
    decoder.prefill(model, policy, &mut seq.state, &seq.tokens, last);
}

/// Where batches run ahead of a request into a sequence that was `base`
/// tokens long stop for `prompt`: on the last multiple of `grid` after
/// `base` before its last token, which a request for it, or for any longer
/// prompt starting with it, may cut at without changing a bit.
pub fn ahead_end(base: usize, prompt: usize, grid: usize) -> usize {
    base + prompt.saturating_sub(base + 1) / grid * grid
}

## 0. Décision structurante : un seul backend complet par API

Le dépôt a aujourd'hui **deux couches par API GPU** :

- CUDA est éclaté entre `kinetic-cuda` (driver, noyaux, lanceurs) et
  `kinetic-models/src/cuda` (orchestration du modèle) ;
- Vulkan est éclaté entre `kinetic-vulkan` (loader, shaders, noyaux) et
  `kinetic-models/src/vulkan` (orchestration du modèle).

La cible est différente et plus simple :

> **Un seul backend complet par API GPU.** Tout CUDA vit dans `kinetic-cuda` :
> driver, noyaux, layouts, graphes, mémoire, exécution du modèle, capacités.
> Tout Vulkan vit dans `kinetic-vulkan`. Le CPU reste le chemin de référence :
> ses noyaux dans `kinetic-cpu`, son exécution générique dans `kinetic-models`.
> `kinetic-models` ne contient plus de code CUDA/Vulkan : il décrit les
> architectures, les blocs et les invariants, et expose une interface
> d'exécution **au niveau modèle** (charger, préfill, décoder, état de
> séquence, capacités), pas au niveau noyau.

Les autres API (HIP, SYCL, WebGPU) sont des **backends de compatibilité** :
chacun est complet pour son API, mais n'est ajouté que lorsqu'une machine et
une CI peuvent le valider. Metal reste un chemin du backend Vulkan
(MoltenVK), pas un backend séparé. L'utilisateur n'en charge qu'un seul à
l'exécution, selon sa carte. On fournit le socle (trait, capacités, tests de
conformance, modèle de build), pas une implémentation complète et
invérifiable de chaque API.

### 0.1 État actuel vs cible

| Aujourd'hui | Cible |
|---|---|
| CUDA : `kinetic-cuda` + `kinetic-models/src/cuda` | `kinetic-cuda` contient tout CUDA |
| Vulkan : `kinetic-vulkan` + `kinetic-models/src/vulkan` | `kinetic-vulkan` contient tout Vulkan |
| `kinetic-models` a des features `cuda` / `vulkan` et des modules backend | `kinetic-models` sans feature backend, expose un trait `ModelRunner` |
| `kinetic-server` a `cuda.rs`, `vulkan.rs`, `cpu.rs` | `kinetic-server` choisit un backend via une factory |
| Ajouter HIP = nouveau crate + nouveau module dans `kinetic-models` | Ajouter HIP = nouveau crate qui implémente `ModelRunner` |
| Les tests modèle connaissent les backends | Les tests modèle utilisent le runner CPU ou un mock |

### 0.2 Où vivent les traits

Deux couches, pas une :

- **`kinetic-runtime`** (à créer) : découverte des devices, registre/factory
  de backends, capacités, budget mémoire, ordonnanceur, pool KV, métriques.
  Il ne connaît **pas** les types de modèle.
- **`kinetic-models`** : architectures, blocs, modèle générique, trait
  `ModelRunner` au niveau modèle, runner CPU de référence.
- **`kinetic-cuda` / `kinetic-vulkan` / `kinetic-hip`** : implémentent
  `ModelRunner` et possèdent leurs noyaux, graphes et politiques de mémoire.
- **`kinetic-server`** : garde le trait `Backend` actuel (requête,
  `reuses`, `run_ahead`, `settle_some`) au-dessus de `ModelRunner`.

Cette séparation évite un cycle de dépendances et évite de transformer
`kinetic-runtime` en compilateur de graphes. Le trait `ModelRunner` reste
petit : charger, préfill, décoder, état de séquence, capacités. Chaque
backend garde la liberté de fusionner, grapher et ordonnancer ses noyaux
comme il veut.

### 0.3 Migration incrémentale

1. Créer `kinetic-runtime` avec les types de devices, capacités, budget
   mémoire et factory. Aucun changement de comportement.
2. Extraire dans `kinetic-models` un trait `ModelRunner` au niveau modèle et
   exposer les descripteurs nécessaires aux backends. Le runner CPU existant
   devient l'implémentation de référence.
3. Déplacer `kinetic-models/src/cuda` vers `kinetic-cuda/src/runner` et
   `kinetic-models/src/vulkan` vers `kinetic-vulkan/src/runner`. Ce n'est pas
   un simple `git mv` : il faut passer par le trait et les descripteurs
   exposés, et conserver les tests à chaque étape.
4. Retirer les features `cuda` / `vulkan` de `kinetic-models` ; il ne dépend
   plus des crates backend.
5. Ajouter une factory de backend dans `kinetic-server` / `kinetic-cli` :
   `auto | cpu | cuda | vulkan | hip`, un seul backend chargé.
6. Ajouter un backend de test (CPU ou mock) pour tester `kinetic-models`
   sans GPU.
7. Seulement ensuite, optimiser. Le refactor d'abord ; la performance vient
   après, avec les mêmes gates d'exactitude.

### 0.4 Contrat de compatibilité d'un backend

Un backend n'est « fourni » que s'il respecte ce contrat :

- **Découverte** : `probe()` liste les devices et leurs capacités réelles.
- **Capacités** : types de poids, formats KV, batch max, async, multi-device,
  mémoire disponible. Le serveur refuse clairement ce qui n'est pas supporté.
- **Conformance** : mêmes tokens que le runner CPU sur le corpus de contrôle,
  aux tolérances près, et mêmes gates d'identité.
- **Mesure** : `kinetic bench` et le protocole A/B fonctionnent sur ce
  backend, avec un seuil de régression.
- **Isolement** : un seul backend est chargé à l'exécution ; les autres ne
  coûtent ni mémoire ni temps de démarrage.
- **CI** : au moins un runner ou une machine de référence valide le backend
  avant qu'il ne soit activé par défaut.

Tant qu'un backend ne passe pas ce contrat, il reste **opt-in** et documenté
comme expérimental. C'est ainsi qu'on fournit les bases de HIP/SYCL/WebGPU
sans promettre une parité invérifiable.

### 0.5 Ce que cela change pour les experts

- **GPU AMD** travaille dans `kinetic-vulkan` et `kinetic-hip`, pas dans
  `kinetic-models`.
- **Runtime** travaille dans `kinetic-runtime` et `kinetic-server`, pas dans
  les crates backend.
- **Rust backend** pilote la migration et garde les seams `Family`,

/// Whether a layer hands its keys and values to later layers or attends
/// over another layer's instead of projecting its own.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SharedKv {
    #[default]
    No,
    /// Keeps each batch's keys and values for the layers that borrow them.
    Lends,
    /// Uses those of the lending layer at this index.
    Borrows(usize),
}

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
pub struct KvCache {
    pub(super) k: Vec<f32>,
    pub(super) v: Vec<f32>,
    /// One entry per row stored since the last checkpoint.
    journal: Option<Vec<Stored>>,
    /// The keys and values of the batch in flight, lent by
    /// [`SharedKv::Lends`] and taken by [`SharedKv::Borrows`].
    pub(crate) lent: Option<(Vec<f32>, Vec<f32>)>,
}

/// A row stored since the checkpoint: its position, keys and values, and
/// how to undo storing it.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct Stored {
    pos: usize,
    k: Vec<f32>,
    v: Vec<f32>,
    undo: Undo,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
enum Undo {
    Appended { len: usize },
    Overwrote { at: usize, k: Vec<f32>, v: Vec<f32> },
}

impl KvCache {
    /// Starts recording changes so [`KvCache::rollback`] can undo them.
    pub fn checkpoint(&mut self) {
        self.journal = Some(Vec::new());
    }

    /// Keeps `rows`, an increasing path through the rows stored since the
    /// checkpoint, as if only they had been stored, and stops recording.
    /// Kept rows need not be contiguous: rows off the path are dropped and
    /// the cache is compacted.
    pub fn rollback(&mut self, rows: &[usize], window: Option<usize>) {
        let Some(journal) = self.journal.take() else {
            return;
        };
        let keep = leading(rows);
        let kept: Vec<&Stored> = rows[keep..].iter().map(|&r| &journal[r]).collect();
        for stored in journal[keep..].iter().rev() {
            match &stored.undo {
                Undo::Appended { len } => {
                    self.k.truncate(*len);
                    self.v.truncate(*len);
                }
                Undo::Overwrote { at, k, v } => {
                    self.k[*at..][..k.len()].copy_from_slice(k);
                    self.v[*at..][..v.len()].copy_from_slice(v);
                }
            }
        }
        for row in kept {
            self.store(window, row.pos, &row.k, &row.v);
        }
    }

    /// Stores the keys and values of position `pos`. A full window is a
    /// ring indexed by `pos % window`; attention does not depend on the
    /// order of positions.
    fn store(&mut self, window: Option<usize>, pos: usize, k: &[f32], v: &[f32]) {
        let kv_dim = k.len();
        let undo = match window {
            Some(w) if self.k.len() == w * kv_dim => {
                let at = (pos % w) * kv_dim;
                let undo = self.journal.is_some().then(|| Undo::Overwrote {
                    at,
                    k: self.k[at..][..kv_dim].to_vec(),
                    v: self.v[at..][..kv_dim].to_vec(),
                });
                self.k[at..][..kv_dim].copy_from_slice(k);
                self.v[at..][..kv_dim].copy_from_slice(v);
                undo
            }
            _ => {
                let len = self.k.len();
                self.k.extend_from_slice(k);
                self.v.extend_from_slice(v);
                Some(Undo::Appended { len })
            }
        };
        if let (Some(journal), Some(undo)) = (&mut self.journal, undo) {
            journal.push(Stored {
                pos,
                k: k.to_vec(),
                v: v.to_vec(),
                undo,
            });
        }
    }
}

impl Attention<'_> {
    /// Runs a batch whose first token sits at position `pos0`. With `grid`,
    /// token `t` rotates by the (time, row, column) position `grid[t]`
    /// instead of by `pos0 + t`. With `tree`, token `t` sits at
    /// `pos0 + tree.depth(t)` and attends only to the cache and its own
    /// path, so each token's output is what running its path alone gives;
    /// the cache then holds every token until [`KvCache::rollback`] keeps
    /// one path.
    pub fn forward(
        &self,
        h: &[f32],
        pos0: usize,
        grid: Option<&[[usize; 3]]>,
        tree: Option<&Tree>,
        cache: &mut KvCache,
    ) -> Vec<f32> {
        let n = h.len() / self.q.cols;
        let mixed = self.mix(self.project(h), n, pos0, grid, tree, cache);
        super::output(&self.o, &mixed)
    }

    /// The queries, keys and values of a batch, biases added, and the
    /// per-head gates when the model has them.
    pub(super) fn project(&self, h: &[f32]) -> Vec<Vec<f32>> {

            matmul(&self.q, h, &mut q);
            return vec![q, Vec::new(), Vec::new()];
        }
        let mut q = vec![0.0; n * self.q.rows];
        let mut k = vec![0.0; n * kv_dim];
        let mut v = vec![0.0; n * kv_dim];
        let mut p = match &self.gate {
            Gate::PerHead(g) => {
                let mut head_gates = vec![0.0; n * self.n_head];
                matmul_many(
                    &[&self.q, &self.k, &self.v, g],
                    h,
                    &mut [&mut q, &mut k, &mut v, &mut head_gates],
                );
                vec![q, k, v, head_gates]
            }
            Gate::Interleaved | Gate::None => {
                matmul_many(
                    &[&self.q, &self.k, &self.v],
                    h,
                    &mut [&mut q, &mut k, &mut v],

                vec![q, k, v]
            }

        for (y, bias) in p.iter_mut().zip([&self.q_bias, &self.k_bias, &self.v_bias]) {

            });
        }
        p
    }

/// Keys and values of one attention layer, as f16: every position, or for
/// a window the last ones in a ring with room for a batch more, so a pass
/// and a rollback never overwrite a position still seen.
pub struct KvCache {
    k: DeviceBuffer<u32>,
    v: DeviceBuffer<u32>,
    positions: usize,
    rows: usize,
    slots: usize,
}

impl KvCache {
    /// A cache for `positions` positions run in passes of up to `rows`.
    pub fn new(
        device: &Rc<Device>,
        shape: &AttentionShape,
        positions: usize,
        rows: usize,
    ) -> Result<KvCache> {
        shape.check()?;
        let slots = shape
            .window
            .map_or(positions, |w| (w + rows).min(positions))
            .max(1);
        let words = slots * shape.kv_dim() / 2;
        Ok(KvCache {
            k: DeviceBuffer::new(device, words)?,
            v: DeviceBuffer::new(device, words)?,
            positions,
            rows,
            slots,
        })
    }

    pub fn positions(&self) -> usize {
        self.positions
    }

    /// Positions stored at once.
    pub fn slots(&self) -> usize {
        self.slots
    }

    /// The keys and values of slots `slots`, as f16 bits.
    pub fn save(&self, slots: Range<usize>) -> Result<(Vec<u16>, Vec<u16>)> {
        let row = self.k.len() / self.slots;
        let read = |b: &DeviceBuffer<u32>| -> Result<Vec<u16>> {
            let mut words = vec![0; slots.len() * row];
            b.copy_range_to(slots.start * row, &mut words)?;
            Ok(words
                .iter()
                .flat_map(|w| [*w as u16, (w >> 16) as u16])
                .collect())
        };
        Ok((read(&self.k)?, read(&self.v)?))
    }

    /// Writes keys and values as [`KvCache::save`] gives them from slot `at`.
    pub fn load(&mut self, at: usize, k: &[u16], v: &[u16]) -> Result<()> {
        let row = self.k.len() / self.slots;
        let words = |x: &[u16]| -> Vec<u32> {
            x.chunks_exact(2)
                .map(|p| u32::from(p[0]) | (u32::from(p[1]) << 16))
                .collect()
        };
        self.k.copy_range_from(at * row, &words(k))?;
        self.v.copy_range_from(at * row, &words(v))
    }

    /// Device bytes held.
    pub fn size_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        8 * self.k.len()
    }
}

    pub data: &'a DeviceBuffer<f32>,
    pub q_norm: Option<usize>,
    pub k_norm: Option<usize>,
    pub bias: Option<usize>,
}

//! How much memory the system can give out.

/// Bytes the system could hand out now without paging, cached file pages
/// included, where the platform reports it.
#[cfg(windows)]
pub fn available() -> Option<u64> {
    #[repr(C)]
    struct MemoryStatus {
        length: u32,
        load: u32,
        total_phys: u64,
        avail_phys: u64,
        total_page_file: u64,
        avail_page_file: u64,
        total_virtual: u64,
        avail_virtual: u64,
        avail_extended_virtual: u64,
    }

    #[link(name = "kernel32")]
    extern "system" {
        fn GlobalMemoryStatusEx(status: *mut MemoryStatus) -> i32;
    }

    let mut status = MemoryStatus {
        length: size_of::<MemoryStatus>() as u32,
        load: 0,
        total_phys: 0,
        avail_phys: 0,
        total_page_file: 0,
        avail_page_file: 0,
        total_virtual: 0,
        avail_virtual: 0,
        avail_extended_virtual: 0,
    };
    // SAFETY: `status` is a MEMORYSTATUSEX with its length set, which the
    // call only writes.
    let ok = unsafe { GlobalMemoryStatusEx(&mut status) };
    (ok != 0).then_some(status.avail_phys)
}

#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]
pub fn available() -> Option<u64> {
    let info = std::fs::read_to_string("/proc/meminfo").ok()?;
    let kib: u64 = info
        .lines()
        .find_map(|l| l.strip_prefix("MemAvailable:"))?
        .trim()
        .strip_suffix("kB")?
        .trim()
        .parse()
        .ok()?;
    Some(kib * 1024)
}

#[cfg(not(any(windows, target_os = "linux")))]
pub fn available() -> Option<u64> {
    None
}

//! Per-layer token inputs, as in Gemma 4: besides the shared embedding,
//! every layer gets a small input of its own, built from a second token
//! table and a projection of the embedding, which it adds back to the
//! residual stream through a gated bottleneck.

use std::f32::consts::FRAC_1_SQRT_2;

use kinetic_cpu::{matmul, pool, rms_norm};
use kinetic_quant::Matrix;

use crate::blocks::gelu;
use crate::model::embed_into;

pub(crate) struct PerLayer<'a> {
    /// `width` values per layer for every token.
    pub embd: Matrix<'a>,
    /// From the scaled embedding to `width` values per layer.
    pub proj: Matrix<'a>,
    pub proj_norm: Vec<f32>,
    pub width: usize,
    pub layers: Vec<LayerInput<'a>>,
}

/// How one layer folds its input into the residual stream.
pub(crate) struct LayerInput<'a> {
    pub gate: Matrix<'a>,
    pub proj: Matrix<'a>,
    pub norm: Vec<f32>,
    /// Multiplies the whole residual stream once the layer is done.
    pub scale: f32,
}

impl PerLayer<'_> {
    /// The inputs of every layer for the rows `x` embedding `tokens`:
    /// `layers * width` values per row, layer by layer.
    pub fn inputs(&self, tokens: &[u32], x: &[f32], eps: f32) -> Vec<f32> {
        let all = self.embd.cols;
        let mut from_token = vec![0.0; tokens.len() * all];
        embed_into(
            &self.embd,
            Some((self.width as f32).sqrt()),
            tokens,
            &mut from_token,
        );
        let mut out = vec![0.0; tokens.len() * all];
        matmul(&self.proj, x, &mut out);
        let scale = 1.0 / (self.proj.cols as f32).sqrt();
        pool::for_each_chunk(&mut out, self.width, |i, row| {
            row.iter_mut().for_each(|v| *v *= scale);
            rms_norm(row, &self.proj_norm, eps);
            let token = &from_token[i * self.width..][..self.width];
            row.iter_mut()
                .zip(token)
                .for_each(|(v, t)| *v = (*v + t) * FRAC_1_SQRT_2);
        });
        out
    }

    /// Adds layer `i`'s input to the rows `x` and applies its scale.
    pub fn apply(&self, i: usize, x: &mut [f32], inputs: &[f32], eps: f32) {
        let l = &self.layers[i];
        let (d, w, n_layer) = (l.proj.rows, self.width, self.layers.len());
        let n = x.len() / d;
        let mut g = vec![0.0; n * w];
        matmul(&l.gate, x, &mut g);
        for (t, row) in g.chunks_exact_mut(w).enumerate() {
            let input = &inputs[(t * n_layer + i) * w..][..w];
            row.iter_mut()
                .zip(input)
                .for_each(|(g, v)| *g = gelu(*g) * v);
        }
        let mut y = vec![0.0; n * d];
        matmul(&l.proj, &g, &mut y);
        pool::for_each_chunk(&mut y, d, |_, row| rms_norm(row, &l.norm, eps));
        pool::for_each_chunk(x, d, |t, row| {
            row.iter_mut()
                .zip(&y[t * d..])
                .for_each(|(x, y)| *x = (*x + y) * l.scale);
        });
    }
}

pub struct AttentionIo<'a> {
    /// [`AttentionShape::q_len`] values per token; rotated in place.
    pub q: &'a mut DeviceBuffer<f32>,
    /// Normalized in place by norms that span all heads.

/// How a [`KvCache`] stores keys or values.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KvType {
    /// f16 values.
    #[default]
    F16,
    /// q8_0: blocks of 32 int8 values times an f16 scale, 34 bytes where f16
    /// takes 64. Attention then reads rounded values, so outputs change.
    Q8_0,
}

/// Values per q8_0 block; head sizes are multiples of it.
const Q8_BLOCK: usize = 32;

enum Store {
    F16(DeviceBuffer<u16>),
    Q8_0 {
        quants: DeviceBuffer<i8>,
        scales: DeviceBuffer<u16>,
    },
}

impl Store {
    fn new(ctx: &Rc<Context>, ty: KvType, len: usize) -> Result<Store> {
        Ok(match ty {
            KvType::F16 => Store::F16(DeviceBuffer::new(ctx, len)?),
            KvType::Q8_0 => Store::Q8_0 {
                quants: DeviceBuffer::new(ctx, len)?,
                scales: DeviceBuffer::new(ctx, len / Q8_BLOCK)?,
            },
        })
    }

    /// The values and the scales, 0 for f16.
    fn ptrs(&self) -> (u64, u64) {
        match self {
            Store::F16(v) => (v.device_ptr(), 0),
            Store::Q8_0 { quants, scales } => (quants.device_ptr(), scales.device_ptr()),
        }
    }

    fn size_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Store::F16(v) => 2 * v.len(),
            Store::Q8_0 { quants, scales } => quants.len() + 2 * scales.len(),
        }
    }

    /// Values `start..start + out.len()`; `start` is a multiple of 32.
    fn save(&self, start: usize, out: &mut [f32]) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            Store::F16(v) => {
                let mut bits = vec![0; out.len()];
                v.copy_range_to(start, &mut bits)?;
                for (o, b) in out.iter_mut().zip(bits) {
                    *o = f16::from_bits(b).to_f32();
                }
            }
            Store::Q8_0 { quants, scales } => {
                let mut q = vec![0; out.len()];
                let mut d = vec![0; out.len() / Q8_BLOCK];
                quants.copy_range_to(start, &mut q)?;
                scales.copy_range_to(start / Q8_BLOCK, &mut d)?;
                for ((out, q), d) in out.chunks_mut(Q8_BLOCK).zip(q.chunks(Q8_BLOCK)).zip(d) {
                    let d = f16::from_bits(d).to_f32();
                    for (o, &q) in out.iter_mut().zip(q) {
                        *o = d * f32::from(q);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Writes `x` at value `start`, a multiple of 32, rounded as the device
    /// rounds; values from [`Store::save`] come back unchanged.
    fn load(&mut self, start: usize, x: &[f32]) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            Store::F16(v) => {
                let bits: Vec<u16> = x.iter().map(|&x| f16::from_f32(x).to_bits()).collect();
                v.copy_range_from(start, &bits)
            }
            Store::Q8_0 { quants, scales } => {
                let mut q = vec![0; x.len()];
                let mut d = vec![0; x.len() / Q8_BLOCK];
                for ((x, q), d) in x.chunks(Q8_BLOCK).zip(q.chunks_mut(Q8_BLOCK)).zip(&mut d) {
                    let scale = x.iter().fold(0.0f32, |m, v| m.max(v.abs())) / 127.0;
                    for (q, &x) in q.iter_mut().zip(x) {
                        *q = if scale == 0.0 {
                            0
                        } else {
                            (x / scale).round_ties_even() as i8
                        };
                    }
                    *d = f16::from_f32(scale).to_bits();
                }
                quants.copy_range_from(start, &q)?;
                scales.copy_range_from(start / Q8_BLOCK, &d)
            }
        }
    }
}

/// A key-value cache, f16 unless asked otherwise. A full cache stores
/// position `p` at slot `p`; a windowed one is a ring of `slots` entries.
pub struct KvCache {
    k: Store,
    v: Store,
    slots: usize,
    kv_dim: usize,
}

impl KvCache {
    /// An f16 cache of `slots` positions for layers of `shape`. A windowed
    /// cache needs more slots than its window by the most tokens that may be
    /// run and then rolled back, since those overwrite the oldest entries.
    pub fn new(ctx: &Rc<Context>, shape: &AttentionShape, slots: usize) -> Result<KvCache> {
        KvCache::with_types(ctx, shape, slots, KvType::F16, KvType::F16)
    }

    /// [`KvCache::new`] with keys stored as `k` and values as `v`.
    pub fn with_types(
        ctx: &Rc<Context>,
        shape: &AttentionShape,
        slots: usize,
        k: KvType,
        v: KvType,
    ) -> Result<KvCache> {
        shape.check()?;
        if shape.window.is_some_and(|w| slots <= w) || u32::try_from(slots).is_err() {
            return Err(Error::Shape(format!(
                "{slots} cache slots for a window of {:?}",
                shape.window
            )));
        }
        let len = slots * shape.kv_dim();
        Ok(KvCache {
            k: Store::new(ctx, k, len)?,
            v: Store::new(ctx, v, len)?,
            slots,
            kv_dim: shape.kv_dim(),
        })
    }

    pub fn slots(&self) -> usize {
        self.slots
    }

    /// Device bytes held.
    pub fn size_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.k.size_bytes() + self.v.size_bytes()
    }

    /// Copies the keys and values of `slots` to the host.
    pub fn save(&self, slots: Range<usize>) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<f32>)> {
        let len = slots.len() * self.kv_dim;
        let (mut k, mut v) = (vec![0.0; len], vec![0.0; len]);
        self.k.save(slots.start * self.kv_dim, &mut k)?;
        self.v.save(slots.start * self.kv_dim, &mut v)?;
        Ok((k, v))
    }

    /// Writes keys and values from [`KvCache::save`] at slot `at` on.
    pub fn load(&mut self, at: usize, k: &[f32], v: &[f32]) -> Result<()> {
        self.k.load(at * self.kv_dim, k)?;
        self.v.load(at * self.kv_dim, v)
    }
}

fn ptr(buf: Option<&DeviceBuffer<f32>>) -> u64 {
