impl Kernels {
    /// Queues a copy of the keys and values `src` holds for the positions
    /// of `batch` into `dst`, a cache of the same shape and slots. The
    /// positions are read on the device, so a recorded graph replays it.
    pub fn copy_kv(
        &self,
        src: &KvCache,
        dst: &mut KvCache,
        batch: &Batch,
        stream: &Stream,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        if src.slots != dst.slots || src.kv_dim != dst.kv_dim {
            return Err(Error::Shape("copy between caches of other shapes".into()));
        }
        let stores = [&src.k, &src.v, &dst.k, &dst.v];
        if stores.iter().any(|s| !matches!(s, Store::F16(_))) {
            return Err(Error::Shape("layers share only f16 caches".into()));
        }
        let kv_dim = src.kv_dim as u32;
        let (b, slots) = (batch.device_ptr(), src.slots as u32);
        let ptrs = stores.map(|s| s.ptrs().0);
        let mut args = [
            arg(&b),
            arg(&ptrs[0]),
            arg(&ptrs[1]),
            arg(&ptrs[2]),
            arg(&ptrs[3]),
            arg(&kv_dim),
            arg(&slots),
        ];
        let config = LaunchConfig {
            grid: [batch.len() as u32, kv_dim.div_ceil(256), 1],
            block: [256, 1, 1],
            shared_bytes: 0,
        };
        // SAFETY: matches `attn_copy_kv(const unsigned*, const __half*,
        // const __half*, __half*, __half*, unsigned, unsigned)`; both caches
        // hold `slots * kv_dim` values and every slot is taken mod `slots`.
        unsafe { self.attn_copy_kv.launch(config, stream, &mut args) }
    }

    /// Queues gated attention for every token of `batch`: normalizes and
    /// rotates queries and keys, stores keys and values in `cache`, attends
    /// each query over its causal (and windowed) past and writes the gated
    /// result to `io.out`.
    ///
    /// Batches of more than [`MAX_BATCH`] tokens run flash-style without
    /// scratch, on tensor cores as accurate as f32 arithmetic and without
    /// them in f32, but summed in another order, so their results differ
    /// slightly from smaller batches. Without tensor cores, heads of 64
    /// store every key and value first, then attend [`MAX_BATCH`] queries at
    /// a time, with the scratch and results of smaller batches. They need
    /// [`Kernels::large_batches`]. A windowed
    /// cache must hold the window and the batch.
    pub fn attention(
        &self,
        params: AttentionParams,
        io: AttentionIo,
        cache: &mut KvCache,
        batch: &Batch,
        stream: &Stream,
    ) -> Result<()> {
        let s = params.shape;
        s.check()?;
        let n = batch.len();
        let (hd, kv_dim) = (s.head_dim, s.kv_dim());
        let width = s.n_head * hd;
        if s.window.is_none() && batch.pos() + n > cache.slots {
            return Err(Error::Shape(format!(
                "positions up to {} in a cache of {}",
                batch.pos() + n,
                cache.slots
            )));
        }
        let spans = |w: Option<&DeviceBuffer<f32>>, heads| match w {
            Some(w) => s.spans_heads(w.len(), heads),
            None => Some(false),
        };
        let (q_rows, k_rows) = (
            spans(params.q_norm, s.n_head),
            spans(params.k_norm, s.n_head_kv),
        );
        let biased = params.q_bias.is_some() || params.k_bias.is_some() || params.v_bias.is_some();
        let bias_fits = |b: Option<&DeviceBuffer<f32>>, len| b.is_none_or(|b| b.len() == len);
        if cache.kv_dim != kv_dim
            || io.out.width() != width
            || q_rows.is_none()
            || k_rows.is_none()
            || (biased && (s.interleaved_gate || q_rows == Some(true) || k_rows == Some(true)))
            || !bias_fits(params.q_bias, width)
            || !bias_fits(params.k_bias, kv_dim)
            || !bias_fits(params.v_bias, kv_dim)
            || params
                .rope_factors
                .is_some_and(|f| f.len() != s.rope_dims / 2)
            || (s.interleaved_gate && io.head_gate.is_some())
        {
            return Err(Error::Shape(format!(
                "attention buffers do not fit shape {s:?}"
            )));
        }
        io.q.check_holds(n * s.q_len(), "attention queries")?;
        if params.store {
            io.k.check_holds(n * kv_dim, "attention keys")?;
            io.v.check_holds(n * kv_dim, "attention values")?;
        }
        if let Some(g) = io.head_gate {
            g.check_holds(n * s.n_head, "attention head gates")?;
        }
        if let Some(w) = s.window {
            if n + w - 1 > cache.slots {
                return Err(Error::Shape(format!(
                    "{n} tokens in a ring of {} for a window of {w}",
                    cache.slots

A model's own prediction block goes to the first GPU, with the embeddings

For now, `--gpus` takes dense models without per-layer inputs or shared
attention caches (not mixture-of-experts models or Gemma 4 E2B/E4B), and
runs the requests of `--parallel` one after another rather than in shared
passes.

## Memory

**Weights are memory-mapped.** Kinetic does not copy the model into its own
memory; the operating system reads the file's pages as they are used and
keeps them in its file cache. On the CPU, a model needs about its file size
in RAM to run at full speed. On the GPU, the weights are copied to video
memory at load time.

**The context sets the cache size.** Each conversation gets a cache for up
to `-c` tokens, 32768 by default (less if the model was trained on less;
`-c 0` takes everything the model supports). On the GPU that cache is
reserved at load time, so a model that does not fit with the default
context may fit with `-c 8192`. Models with recurrent layers (Qwen3.5,
LFM2, LFM3, Granite 4.0 H, Falcon-H1) need much less cache per token than
pure transformers.

**A quantized cache holds about twice the context.** On CUDA,
`--cache-type-k q8_0` and `--cache-type-v q8_0` (llama.cpp's `-ctk` and
`-ctv`) store keys and values in blocks of 32 int8 values with one f16
scale, 34 bytes where f16 takes 64. Every token stays in the cache, but its
keys and values are rounded, so answers differ from the f16 cache's: close
in quality, not identical, and never what the exactness checks compare
against. It is off by default. The CPU and Vulkan paths ignore it.

**Warm Start keeps prompt states** in up to 1 GiB of RAM and 2 GiB on disk,
under `--cache-dir` (by default `kinetic/warm` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on
Windows and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache` on Linux and macOS). `--no-prompt-cache`
turns it off.

`kinetic bench` reports the peak memory of a run.

## Mixture-of-experts offload

A mixture-of-experts model that does not fit in GPU memory still runs on the
GPU with `--device auto` or `cuda`. Kinetic puts the attention layers, the
shared weights and the cache on the GPU, gives the remaining free memory to
a cache of experts, and leaves the other experts in the memory-mapped file.
Each layer then runs the experts it picks where that is cheapest at the
moment: from the GPU cache, on the CPU, or copied over. See
[Flywheel](how-it-is-fast.md#flywheel) for how it decides.

For this to be fast, the whole file should fit in system RAM next to your
other programs. Kinetic reads the experts into memory at load time when they
fit with 3 GiB to spare, and otherwise lets the first tokens read them as
needed.

When every expert fits on the GPU, there is no offload: routing runs on the
GPU too.

### Runtime options

`run`, `chat` and `serve` take these:

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-c`, `--ctx-size <N>` | most tokens per conversation, prompt and answer together; 0 uses all the model supports [default: 32768, or less if the model was trained on less, or if its cache would not fit beside the model on the GPU] |
| `-t`, `--threads <N>` | CPU threads [default: all] |
| `--device <auto\|cpu\|cuda\|vulkan>` | where the model runs; `auto` tries CUDA, then Vulkan, then the CPU [default: auto]; see [Devices](devices.md) |
| `--gpu-layers <N>` | most layers on the GPU, the rest on the CPU [default: as many as fit]; see [Devices](devices.md#dense-models-larger-than-the-gpu) |
| `--gpus <LIST>` | CUDA GPUs to spread the layers over, such as `0,1`; the first also holds the embeddings and output head [default: 0]; see [Devices](devices.md#several-gpus) |
| `--cache-dir <DIR>` | where Warm Start keeps prompt states [default: `kinetic/warm` in the user's cache directory] |
| `--no-prompt-cache` | run every prompt from its first token; same as `--off warm-start` |
| `--off <LIST>` | turn speed technologies off, comma-separated: `rad1`, `warm-start`, `zero-wait`, `shortlist`, `torque`, `convoy` |
| `--cache-type-k <f16\|q8_0>`, `--cache-type-v <f16\|q8_0>` | how the CUDA cache stores keys and values; `q8_0` takes about half the memory but changes outputs [default: f16]; see [Devices](devices.md#memory) |
| `--rope-scaling <none\|linear\|yarn>` | rotary scaling for contexts longer than the model was trained on; overrides the file |
| `--rope-scale <N>` | context stretch factor (`--rope-freq-scale` takes its inverse, as llama.cpp does) |
| `--rope-freq-base <N>` | rotary base, for NTK-aware scaling |
| `--yarn-orig-ctx <N>` | the context the model was trained on, for YaRN |
| `--sign-key <FILE>` | sign [receipts](receipts.md) with this Ed25519 secret key, 32 bytes or 64 hex digits |
| `--mlock` | keep the model in RAM, so the system never swaps it out (GGUF files) |
| `--no-mmap` | read the model into memory instead of mapping the file (GGUF files) |
| `--chat-template-file <FILE>` | Jinja chat template to use instead of the model's own |
| `--lora <FILE>[,<FILE>...]` | LoRA adapters in llama.cpp's GGUF format, merged into the weights at load |
| `--lora-scaled <FILE>:<SCALE>[,...]` | the same with scales; `--lora-scaled FILE SCALE`, as older llama.cpp builds took it, works too |

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]
enum CacheType {
    F16,
    #[value(name = "q8_0")]
    Q8_0,
}

#[cfg(feature = "cuda")]
impl From<CacheType> for kinetic_cuda::KvType {
    fn from(t: CacheType) -> Self {
        match t {
            CacheType::F16 => kinetic_cuda::KvType::F16,
            CacheType::Q8_0 => kinetic_cuda::KvType::Q8_0,
        }
    }
}

/// Rotary scaling, as llama.cpp spells it; unset values keep the model's.
#[derive(Args)]
struct RopeArgs {
    /// Rotary scaling for contexts past the trained length [default: the model's]
    #[arg(long, value_enum, value_name = "KIND")]
    rope_scaling: Option<RopeKind>,
    /// How many times the trained context rotary positions stretch to
    #[arg(long, value_name = "N", conflicts_with = "rope_freq_scale")]
    rope_scale: Option<f32>,
    /// One over --rope-scale
        }
        None => engine,
    };

        &engine,
        &device,
        &tech::status(&runtime.turned_off(), kind, &Tech::ALL),
    )
}

/// `wanted`, or when its cache would not fit beside the model on the CUDA
/// GPU, the largest context that does, said in one line; otherwise layers
/// would quietly move to the CPU.
fn gpu_context(model: &Model, header: &Gguf, runtime: &RuntimeArgs, wanted: usize) -> usize {
    let gpu = cfg!(feature = "cuda") && matches!(runtime.device, Device::Auto | Device::Cuda);
    let weights = fit::Weights::of(header);
    // experts leave the GPU by design, --gpu-layers asked for a split and
    // --gpus for several GPUs, which this does not add up
    if !gpu || runtime.gpu_layers.is_some() || runtime.gpus.len() > 1 || weights.has_experts() {
        return wanted;
    }
    let Some(free) = system::cuda_free() else {
        return wanted;
    };
    // state_bytes counts f32; the GPU keeps attention caches in --cache-type-*
    let share = |t: CacheType| match t {
        CacheType::F16 => 0.5,
        CacheType::Q8_0 => 34.0 / 128.0,
    };
    let share = (share(runtime.cache_type_k) + share(runtime.cache_type_v)) / 2.0;
    let fixed = model.state_bytes(0) as u64;
    let cache = |n| fixed + ((model.state_bytes(n) as u64 - fixed) as f64 * share) as u64;
    match fit::gpu_context(wanted, free, weights.total(), cache) {
        Some(n) => {
            eprintln!(
                "kinetic: context {}k to fit the GPU; -c to change",
                n / 1024
            );
            n
        }
        None => wanted,
    }
}

/// Layers that run on a further device, after those of the device before.
/// The batch, the stream and its norm come over from that device; the last
/// shard's normalized stream goes back to the main device for the head.
struct Shard {
    gpu: Gpu,
    layers: Vec<CudaLayer>,
    /// The input norm of this shard's first layer, on the device before,
    /// whose last layer applies it.
    entry_norm: Option<DeviceBuffer<f32>>,
    /// The output norm, on this device, which the last shard's last layer
    /// applies.
    output_norm: DeviceBuffer<f32>,
}

impl Gpu {
    fn new(ctx: Rc<Context>) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<Gpu> {
        Ok(Gpu {
            kernels: Kernels::load(&ctx)?,
            stream: Stream::new(&ctx)?,
            side: Stream::new(&ctx)?,
            fork: Event::new(&ctx)?,
            join: Event::new(&ctx)?,
            handoff: Event::new(&ctx)?,
            copied: Event::new(&ctx)?,
            cache: [KvType::F16; 2],
            ctx,
        })
    }

    /// Lets work queued on `side` from now on start on what `stream` has
    /// queued so far.
    fn fork(&self) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
        self.fork.record(&self.stream)?;
            .map(DeviceMatrix::size_bytes)
            .sum()
    }

    /// A cache for `capacity` positions run in batches of up to `rows`; a
    /// windowed one keeps the window plus room for a batch, which also
    /// covers the tokens run since a checkpoint.
    pub fn new_cache(
        &self,
        gpu: &Gpu,
        capacity: usize,
        rows: usize,
    ) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<KvCache> {
        let slots = self.shape.window.map_or(capacity, |w| w + rows);
        let [k, v] = gpu.cache;
        KvCache::with_types(&gpu.ctx, &self.shape, slots, k, v)
    }

    pub fn needs(&self, slots: usize) -> Needs {
        let s = &self.shape;
        let kv = s.n_head_kv * s.head_dim;
        Needs {
            proj: [s.q_len(), kv, kv, s.n_head],
            scratch: s.scratch_len(MAX_BATCH, slots),
            width: s.n_head * s.head_dim,
        }
    }

    /// Reads `s.h` and leaves the projected output in `s.y`.
    pub fn forward(
        &self,
        gpu: &Gpu,
        s: &mut Scratch,
        cache: &mut KvCache,
        batch: &Batch,
    ) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
        self.project(gpu, s, batch.len())?;
        self.mix(gpu, s, cache, batch)?;
        self.output(gpu, s, batch.len())
    }

type Placed<'a> = (Vec<Box<dyn Backend + 'a>>, String);

/// Backends on the device `runtime` asks for, `parallel` of them or as many
/// as memory allows, the device's description and its kind.
fn backend<'a>(
    model: &'a Model<'a>,
    path: &Path,
    runtime: &RuntimeArgs,
    context: usize,
    parallel: Option<usize>,
) -> Result<(Placed<'a>, Device)> {
    let picked = gpu::pick(runtime.device, |kind| match kind {
        Device::Cuda => cuda_backend(model, path, runtime, context, parallel),
        _ => vulkan_backend(model, path, runtime, context),
    })?;
    if let Some(gpu) = picked {
        return Ok(gpu);
    }
    let rad1 = !runtime.is_off(Tech::Rad1);
    let new = || match rad1 {
        true => CpuBackend::new(model),
        false => CpuBackend::new(model).without_drafts(),
    };
    let cpu = match warm_cache(model, path, runtime, None) {
        Some(w) => new().with_warm(w),
        None => new(),
    };
    let slots = parallel.unwrap_or_else(|| default_slots(model, context));
    // states grow as conversations do, so a context that cannot fit only fails much later
    let need = model.state_bytes(context) as u64 * slots as u64;
    if let Some(free) = kinetic_models::memory::available().filter(|&free| need > free) {
        eprintln!(
            "kinetic: {slots} full {context}-token conversations need {:.1} GiB, more than the {:.1} GiB free; lower -c or --parallel if long ones run out of memory",
            need as f64 / (1u64 << 30) as f64,
            free as f64 / (1u64 << 30) as f64
        );
    }
    let mut backends: Vec<Box<dyn Backend + 'a>> = vec![Box::new(cpu)];
    backends.extend((1..slots).map(|_| Box::new(new()) as Box<dyn Backend>));
    Ok(((backends, CPU.into()), Device::Cpu))
}

#[cfg(feature = "cuda")]
fn cuda_backend<'a>(
    model: &'a Model<'a>,
    path: &Path,
    runtime: &RuntimeArgs,
    context: usize,
    parallel: Option<usize>,
) -> Option<std::result::Result<Placed<'a>, kinetic_models::LoadError>> {
    let placement = kinetic_models::cuda::Placement {
        gpu_layers: runtime.gpu_layers,
        devices: runtime.gpus.clone(),
        eager: runtime.is_off(Tech::Torque),
        cache_k: runtime.cache_type_k.into(),
        cache_v: runtime.cache_type_v.into(),
        ..kinetic_models::cuda::Placement::default()
    };
    let gpu = match kinetic_server::CudaBackend::with_placement(model, context, placement) {
        Ok(gpu) if runtime.is_off(Tech::Rad1) => gpu.without_drafts(),
        Ok(gpu) => gpu,
        Err(e) => return Some(Err(e)),
    };
    let name = gpu.device().to_owned();
    let mut slots: Vec<Box<dyn Backend + 'a>> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 1..parallel.unwrap_or(MAX_DEFAULT_SLOTS) {
        match gpu.slot() {
            Ok(slot) => slots.push(Box::new(slot)),
            Err(e) if parallel.is_some() => {
                let e = format!("--parallel {}: {e}", slots.len() + 2);
                return Some(Err(kinetic_models::LoadError(e)));
            }
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
    let gpu = match warm_cache(model, path, runtime, Some("cuda")) {
        Some(w) => gpu.with_warm(w),
        None => gpu,
    };
    slots.insert(0, Box::new(gpu));
    Some(Ok((slots, name)))
}

#[cfg(not(feature = "cuda"))]
fn cuda_backend<'a>(
    _model: &'a Model<'a>,
    _path: &Path,
    _runtime: &RuntimeArgs,
    _context: usize,
    _parallel: Option<usize>,
) -> Option<std::result::Result<Placed<'a>, kinetic_models::LoadError>> {
    None
}

#[cfg(feature = "vulkan")]
fn vulkan_backend<'a>(
    model: &'a Model<'a>,
    path: &Path,
    runtime: &RuntimeArgs,
    context: usize,
) -> Option<std::result::Result<Placed<'a>, kinetic_models::LoadError>> {
    Some(
        kinetic_server::VulkanBackend::new(model, context).map(|gpu| {
            let gpu = match runtime.is_off(Tech::Rad1) {
                true => gpu.without_drafts(),
                false => gpu,
            };
            let name = gpu.device().to_owned();
            let gpu = match warm_cache(model, path, runtime, Some("vulkan")) {
                Some(w) => gpu.with_warm(w),
                None => gpu,
            };
            (vec![Box::new(gpu) as Box<dyn Backend>], name)
        }),
    )
}

    _path: &Path,
    _runtime: &RuntimeArgs,
    _context: usize,

    None
}

fn device<T>(r: kinetic_vulkan::Result<T>) -> T {
    r.unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("Vulkan: {e}"))
}

impl<'a> Run<VulkanModel<'a>> for VulkanBackend<'a> {
    fn run<P: Policy<VulkanModel<'a>>>(
        &mut self,
        prompt: &[u32],
        job: &Job,
        policy: &mut P,
        emit: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u32]) -> bool,
    ) -> Timings {
        let start = Instant::now();
        let (mut seq, cached_tokens, keep) = self.prefill(prompt, policy);
        let prefill = start.elapsed();

        let start = Instant::now();
        let generated = sequence::decode(&self.gpu, &mut self.decoder, policy, &mut seq, job, emit);
        let decode = start.elapsed();
        if let (Some(warm), Some(k)) = (self.warm.as_mut(), keep) {
            // kept in memory either way; a failed disk write only means the
            // next run starts colder
            let _ = warm.insert(&k.tokens, &k.state, &k.logits);
        }
        self.cached = Some(seq);
        Timings {
            prompt_tokens: prompt.len(),
            cached_tokens,
            prefill,
            generated,
            decode,
        }
    }
}

impl Backend for VulkanBackend<'_> {
    fn generate(
        &mut self,
        prompt: &[u32],
        job: &Job,
        emit: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u32]) -> bool,
    ) -> Timings {
        if job.images.is_empty() {
            sequence::generate(self, prompt, job, emit)
        } else {
            self.cpu.generate(prompt, job, emit)
        }
    }
}

Key findings:
- CUDA supports q8_0 KV; Vulkan f16 only.
- CUDA supports multiple slots sharing one `Arc<CudaModel>`; Vulkan creates one backend only (no parallel slots). So `--parallel` on Vulkan is ignored? `vulkan_backend` doesn't take `parallel`, returns one backend. This means Vulkan server concurrency is 1. Important for KV cache analysis: no per-sequence KV pool on Vulkan, one backend.
- CPU creates `slots` backends, each with its own `Model` reference and `State` (KV f32) allocated lazily? `CpuBackend::new` uses `Model` and `State`; `State` likely allocated on first sequence. `state_bytes` estimates. CPU KV is f32, contiguous per sequence, grows as conversation does (Vec extend). No pool, no paged.
- CUDA `CudaModel` shares weights; `new_state()` allocates KV per sequence at full context? `CudaAttention::new_cache(gpu, capacity, rows)` uses `capacity` = context, so each slot reserves full context KV at load. `CudaBackend::slot()` checks free memory. No paged KV; contiguous per sequence, full context. `--parallel` creates N full KV caches; memory = N * context * KV size. This is a big limitation.
- Vulkan `KvCache::new` allocates full context at load; one backend.
- CUDA has q8_0 KV, but `copy_kv` for shared layers only supports f16. So shared KV + q8_0 incompatible. Important.
- CUDA has `KvType::Q8_0` but no q4_0; Vulkan none.
- KV cache is per-layer contiguous, no block table, no prefix sharing between sequences (Warm cache is host-side prefix cache, restores states, not shared KV pages).
- Warm cache stores host states (f32? `HostState`) on disk, up to 1 GiB RAM + 2 GiB disk. It's a prefix cache at sequence level, not paged. It saves/restores full KV for a prefix. Could be large and slow; `warm` has `GRID=256`, `MAX_GRID=8192`, marks for recurrent layers.

/// Everything a sequence carries between calls. A clone is an exact copy
/// that continues independently.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct State {
    pub(crate) pos: usize,
    checkpoint: Option<usize>,
    pub(crate) layers: Vec<MixerState>,
    /// Earlier lengths [`Model::truncate`] can return to, oldest first.
    pub(crate) marks: Vec<Mark>,
    /// For every image run with grid positions: the length after it, and
    /// how far rotary positions then lag behind the length.
    pub(crate) image_shifts: Vec<(usize, usize)>,
}

/// A copy, at one length, of every layer state that cannot be cut back in
/// place; `None` for the others.
#[derive(Clone)]
pub(crate) struct Mark {
    pub pos: usize,
    pub layers: Vec<Option<MixerState>>,
}

impl State {
    /// A state of no layers, which holds the place of one that is away in
    /// a shared pass.
    fn placeholder() -> State {
        State {
            pos: 0,
            checkpoint: None,
            layers: Vec::new(),
            marks: Vec::new(),
            image_shifts: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Number of tokens processed so far.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.pos
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.pos == 0
    }

    /// How far the rotary position of the next token lags behind
    /// [`State::len`].
    pub(crate) fn rope_shift(&self) -> usize {
        self.image_shifts.last().map_or(0, |s| s.1)
    }

    /// The lengths saved by [`Model::mark`], oldest first.
    pub fn marks(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize> + '_ {
        self.marks.iter().map(|m| m.pos)
    }

    /// Drops every mark, so [`Model::truncate`] returns only to the current
    /// length or zero, unless every layer cuts back in place.
    pub fn forget_marks(&mut self) {
        self.marks.clear();
    }
}

/// The result of running a batch: logits for the requested rows and the
/// normalized final hidden state of every token.
pub struct Forward {
    pub logits: Vec<f32>,
    pub hidden: Vec<f32>,
}

/// The cache of a model's prediction block, one entry per position fed.
pub struct MtpState {
    len: usize,
    cache: MixerState,
}

impl MtpState {
    /// Number of positions fed so far.
    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
        self.len
    }

    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
        self.len == 0

    pub fn new_state(&self) -> MixerState {
        match self {
            Mixer::Attention(_) => MixerState::Attention(KvCache::default()),
            Mixer::DeltaNet(d) => MixerState::DeltaNet(d.new_state()),
            Mixer::ShortConv(s) => MixerState::ShortConv(s.new_state()),
            Mixer::Mamba2(m) => MixerState::Mamba2(m.new_state()),
            Mixer::Parallel(ms) => MixerState::Parallel(ms.iter().map(Mixer::new_state).collect()),
        }
    }

    /// Bytes of the state of a sequence `len` tokens long.
    pub fn state_bytes(&self, len: usize) -> usize {
        let floats = match self {
            Mixer::Attention(a) => {
                2 * a.n_head_kv * a.head_dim * a.window.map_or(len, |w| w.min(len))
            }
            Mixer::DeltaNet(d) => {
                d.n_v_heads * d.head_v_dim * d.head_k_dim + d.qkv.rows * (d.conv_taps - 1)
            }
            Mixer::ShortConv(s) => s.out_proj.cols * (s.taps - 1),
            Mixer::Mamba2(m) => m.inner() * m.d_state + m.channels() * (m.conv_taps - 1),
            Mixer::Parallel(ms) => return ms.iter().map(|m| m.state_bytes(len)).sum(),
        };
        floats * size_of::<f32>()
    }

    /// Keeps `rows`, an increasing path through the tokens run since the
    /// last checkpoint, and undoes the rest.
    pub fn rollback(&self, state: &mut MixerState, rows: &[usize]) {
        match (self, state) {
            (Mixer::Attention(a), MixerState::Attention(c)) => c.rollback(rows, a.window),
            (Mixer::DeltaNet(d), MixerState::DeltaNet(s)) => d.rollback(s, rows),
            (Mixer::ShortConv(_), MixerState::ShortConv(s)) => s.rollback(rows),
            (Mixer::Mamba2(m), MixerState::Mamba2(s)) => m.rollback(s, rows),
            (Mixer::Parallel(ms), MixerState::Parallel(ss)) => {
                ms.iter().zip(ss).for_each(|(m, s)| m.rollback(s, rows))
            }
            _ => unreachable!("state does not belong to this mixer"),
        }
    }

    /// Bytes of the state of a sequence `len` tokens long.
    pub fn state_bytes(&self, len: usize) -> usize {
        self.layers.iter().map(|l| l.mixer.state_bytes(len)).sum()
    }

    /// An empty state for a new sequence.
    pub fn new_state(&self) -> State {
        State {
            pos: 0,
            checkpoint: None,
            layers: self.layers.iter().map(|l| l.mixer.new_state()).collect(),
            marks: Vec::new(),
            image_shifts: Vec::new(),
        }
    }

    /// Runs one token and returns the logits for the next.
    pub fn forward(&self, state: &mut State, token: u32) -> Vec<f32> {
        self.forward_batch(state, &[token])
    }

    /// Runs `tokens` in order and returns the logits after the last one.
    /// Weights are read once per batch, so prompts should go through here
    /// rather than token by token.
    pub fn forward_batch(&self, state: &mut State, tokens: &[u32]) -> Vec<f32> {
        self.run(state, tokens, false).logits
    }
        state.marks.retain(|m| m.pos <= state.pos);
        state.image_shifts.retain(|&(end, _)| end <= state.pos);
    }

    /// Saves what [`Model::truncate`] needs to return to the current length
    /// later: a copy of each recurrent or windowed layer state. Attention
    /// caches of every position are cut back instead, so on a model made of
    /// only those a mark costs nothing.
    pub fn mark(&self, state: &mut State) {
        assert!(state.checkpoint.is_none(), "mark inside a checkpoint");
        if state.marks.last().is_some_and(|m| m.pos == state.pos) {
            return;
        }
        let layers = self
            .layers
            .iter()
            .zip(&state.layers)
            .map(|(l, s)| l.mixer.needs_mark().then(|| s.clone()))
            .collect();
        state.marks.push(Mark {
            pos: state.pos,
            layers,
        });
    }

    /// The longest length up to `len` that [`Model::truncate`] returns
    /// `state` to: `len` itself when every layer cuts back in place,
    /// otherwise the latest mark at or before it, or zero.
    pub fn reach(&self, state: &State, len: usize) -> usize {
        let len = len.min(state.pos);
        let in_place = self
            .layers
            .iter()
            .all(|l| l.mixer.truncates_in_place(state.pos));
        if len == state.pos || in_place {
            return len;
        }
        state
            .marks
            .iter()
            .map(|m| m.pos)
            .filter(|&p| p <= len)
            .max()
            .unwrap_or(0)
    }

    /// Returns `state` to the length [`Model::reach`] gives for `len` and
    /// returns that length. Every value left is exactly what the batches
    /// that ran those tokens produced; marks after the length are dropped.
    pub fn truncate(&self, state: &mut State, len: usize) -> usize {
        assert!(state.checkpoint.is_none(), "truncate inside a checkpoint");
        let to = self.reach(state, len);
        if to == state.pos {
            return to;
        }
        if to == 0 {
            *state = self.new_state();
            return 0;
        }
        let mark = state.marks.iter().position(|m| m.pos == to);
        for (i, (layer, ls)) in self.layers.iter().zip(&mut state.layers).enumerate() {
            match mark.and_then(|m| state.marks[m].layers[i].as_ref()) {
                Some(saved) => *ls = saved.clone(),
                None => layer.mixer.truncate(ls, to),
            }
        }
        state.marks.retain(|m| m.pos <= to);
        state.image_shifts.retain(|&(end, _)| end <= to);
        state.pos = to;
        to
    }

//! Cached states on disk, one file per entry. Files are written under a
//! temporary name and renamed, so a reader never sees half a file, and any
//! of them can be deleted at any time; the oldest go first once the
//! directory outgrows its budget.

use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::io::{self, BufReader, BufWriter};
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::sync::Arc;
use std::thread::{self, JoinHandle};
use std::time::SystemTime;

use super::codec::{self, invalid, Reader, Writer, MAX_TOKENS};
use super::{hash::Hasher, Entry, Meta, Saved};
use crate::Model;

const MAGIC: u64 = u64::from_le_bytes(*b"KNWARM\0\0");
/// Bump whenever the layout of a file changes; older files are then skipped
/// and age out.
const VERSION: u64 = 1;
const EXT: &str = "kwarm";
const TEMP_EXT: &str = "kwarm-tmp";

pub struct Disk {
    dir: PathBuf,
    budget: u64,
    model_id: u64,
    /// The usable files for this model.
    pub files: Vec<Indexed>,
    /// The file being written in the background, if any.
    writing: Option<JoinHandle<()>>,
}

/// A cache file: where it is, what it holds and its size.
pub struct Indexed {
    pub path: PathBuf,
    pub meta: Meta,
    pub bytes: usize,
}

impl Disk {
    /// Opens `dir`, creating it readable by the current user only, and
    /// indexes the files written for `model_id` from their headers.
    pub fn open(dir: PathBuf, budget: u64, model_id: u64) -> io::Result<Disk> {
        create_private_dir(&dir)?;
        let mut files = Vec::new();
        for (path, len, _) in cache_files(&dir)? {
            if path.extension().is_some_and(|e| e == EXT) {
                if let Ok(meta) = read_header(&path, model_id) {
                    files.push(Indexed {
                        path,
                        meta,
                        bytes: len as usize,
                    });
                }
            }
        }
        Ok(Disk {
            dir,
            budget,
            model_id,
            files,
            writing: None,
        })
    }

    /// Writes `saved`, which `meta` describes and which takes `bytes` in
    /// memory, in the background, then drops
    /// the files it covers and trims the directory to its budget. The index
    /// takes the file at once; one whose write failed is dropped when a
    /// read of it fails.
    pub fn save(&mut self, meta: &Meta, saved: &Arc<Saved>, bytes: usize) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.wait();
        let mut key = Hasher::default();
        key.word(self.model_id);
        meta.tokens.iter().for_each(|&t| key.word(t.into()));
        let path = self.dir.join(format!("{:016x}.{EXT}", key.finish()));
        let temp = path.with_extension(format!("{}.{TEMP_EXT}", std::process::id()));

        let (covered, kept): (Vec<_>, Vec<_>) = self
            .files
            .drain(..)
            .filter(|f| f.path != path)
            .partition(|f| meta.covers(&f.meta));
        self.files = kept;
        self.files.push(Indexed {
            path: path.clone(),
            meta: meta.clone(),
            bytes,
        });
        let (dir, budget, model_id) = (self.dir.clone(), self.budget, self.model_id);
        let (meta, saved) = (meta.clone(), Arc::clone(saved));
        self.writing = Some(thread::Builder::new().spawn(move || {
            let written =
                write_entry(&temp, model_id, &meta, &saved).and_then(|()| fs::rename(&temp, &path));
            if written.is_err() {
                let _ = fs::remove_file(&temp);
                return;
            }
            for f in covered {
                let _ = fs::remove_file(&f.path);
            }
            let _ = trim(&dir, budget);
        })?);
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Reads file `i` in full. A file that fails its checks is deleted.
    pub fn load(&mut self, i: usize, model: &Model) -> io::Result<Entry> {
        self.wait();

//! The byte form of a [`State`]: little-endian words with a running
//! checksum, every length checked against the model before anything is
//! allocated. An open checkpoint is not part of it.

use std::io::{self, Read, Write};

use super::hash::Hasher;
use crate::blocks::{Mixer, MixerState};
use crate::model::Mark;
use crate::{Model, State};

/// Longest sequence a stored state may claim, far beyond any context.
pub const MAX_TOKENS: usize = 1 << 26;

const CHUNK: usize = 1 << 16;

pub fn invalid(what: &str) -> io::Error {
    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidData, what)
}

pub struct Writer<W> {
    inner: W,
    hash: Hasher,
}

impl<W: Write> Writer<W> {
    pub fn new(inner: W) -> Self {
        Writer {
            inner,
            hash: Hasher::default(),
        }
    }

    pub fn u64(&mut self, v: u64) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.hash.word(v);
        self.inner.write_all(&v.to_le_bytes())
    }

    pub fn u32s(&mut self, v: &[u32]) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.words(v.len(), v.iter().copied())
    }

    pub fn f32s(&mut self, v: &[f32]) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.words(v.len(), v.iter().map(|x| x.to_bits()))
    }

    fn words(&mut self, len: usize, words: impl Iterator<Item = u32>) -> io::Result<()> {
        self.u64(len as u64)?;
        let mut buf = Vec::with_capacity(CHUNK);
        for w in words {
            self.hash.word(w.into());
            buf.extend_from_slice(&w.to_le_bytes());
            if buf.len() == CHUNK {
                self.inner.write_all(&buf)?;
                buf.clear();
            }
        }
        self.inner.write_all(&buf)
    }

    /// Appends the checksum of everything written and returns the sink.
    pub fn finish(mut self) -> io::Result<W> {
        let sum = self.hash.finish();
        self.inner.write_all(&sum.to_le_bytes())?;
        Ok(self.inner)
    }
}

pub struct Reader<R> {
    inner: R,
    hash: Hasher,
}

impl<R: Read> Reader<R> {
    pub fn new(inner: R) -> Self {
        Reader {
            inner,
            hash: Hasher::default(),
        }
    }

    /// Whether every length `old` returns to is also reachable from here.
    fn covers(&self, old: &Meta) -> bool {
        let n = old.tokens.len();
        self.tokens.starts_with(&old.tokens)
            && (self.in_place || !old.in_place)
            && old.marks.iter().chain([&n]).all(|&m| self.reach(m) == m)
    }

    /// The tokens of `prompt` a warm start from this entry skips, a
    /// multiple of `align`. Running at least one token is needed for
    /// logits, unless the entry is the whole prompt and has them.
    fn hit(&self, prompt: &[u32], align: usize) -> usize {
        let common = common_prefix(&self.tokens, prompt);
        if common == prompt.len() && self.tokens.len() == prompt.len() {
            return common;
        }
        let mut len = common.min(prompt.len() - 1);
        loop {
            let reached = self.reach(len / align * align);
            if reached.is_multiple_of(align) {
                return reached;
            }
            len = reached;
        }
    }
}

struct Entry {
    meta: Meta,
    /// Shared with a disk write still running.
    saved: Arc<Saved>,
    bytes: usize,
    used: u64,
}

struct Saved {
    state: State,
    /// Logits after the last token.
    logits: Vec<f32>,
}

impl Entry {
    fn new(meta: Meta, state: State, logits: Vec<f32>) -> Entry {
        let bytes = codec::state_bytes(&state) + 4 * (logits.len() + meta.tokens.len());
        Entry {
            meta,
            saved: Arc::new(Saved { state, logits }),
            bytes,
            used: 0,
        }
    }
}

/// Seconds per byte of reading a cached state from disk before any read
/// has been timed.
const LOAD_RATE: f64 = 1.0 / 5e8;

/// A prefix cache of exact model states for one model.
pub struct Warm<'m> {
    model: &'m Model<'m>,
    model_id: u64,
    grid: Option<usize>,
    /// Batches start at multiples of this, and so do warm starts.
    align: usize,
    /// Aligned batches a runner is handed at once.
    batches_per_call: usize,
    budget: usize,
    clock: u64,
    entries: Vec<Entry>,
    disk: Option<Disk>,
    /// Seconds per token of the latest prefill.
    rate: f64,
    /// Measured seconds per byte of restoring a state on the runner, and of
    /// reading one from disk.
    restore_rate: Option<f64>,
    load_rate: f64,
}

impl<'m> Warm<'m> {
    /// An empty cache for `model` holding up to `memory_bytes` of states.
    /// `model_id` must identify the model file and the code that runs it;
    /// see [`model_id`].
    pub fn new(model: &'m Model<'m>, model_id: u64, memory_bytes: usize) -> Warm<'m> {
        Warm {
            model,
            model_id,
            grid: grid(model),
            align: 1,
            batches_per_call: 1,
            budget: memory_bytes,
            clock: 0,
            entries: Vec::new(),
            disk: None,
            rate: 0.0,
            restore_rate: None,
            load_rate: LOAD_RATE,
        }
    }

    /// Also keeps every inserted entry in `dir`, up to `budget` bytes, and
    /// finds those of earlier runs there. See [`default_dir`].
    pub fn with_disk(mut self, dir: impl Into<PathBuf>, budget: u64) -> io::Result<Self> {
        self.disk = Some(Disk::open(dir.into(), budget, self.model_id)?);
        Ok(self)
    }

    /// Runs prompts in batches of at most `tokens` that start at multiples
    /// of it, and resumes only at such multiples or from an identical
    /// prompt. A warm start then runs exactly the batches of a cold run cut
    /// at those multiples, so it gives the same results on every model,
    /// including those whose results depend on where batches start.
    pub fn aligned(mut self, tokens: usize) -> Self {
        self.align = tokens.max(1);
        self.grid = self.grid.map(|g| g.next_multiple_of(self.align));
        self
    }

    /// Hands the runner up to `batches` aligned batches in one call rather
    /// than one, for runners that cut a call into the same batches and can
    /// overlap them, such as a model split over several GPUs.
    pub fn batches_per_call(mut self, batches: usize) -> Self {
        self.batches_per_call = batches.max(1);
        self
    }

    /// Bytes of states held in memory.
    pub fn memory_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.entries.iter().map(|e| e.bytes).sum()
    }

    /// The number of positions between the marks of a recurrent model, or
    /// `None` when its caches cut back anywhere.
    pub fn grid(&self) -> Option<usize> {
        self.grid
    }

    fn new_work(&self, rows: usize) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<Work> {
        let layers: Vec<&CudaLayer> = self.layers.iter().collect();

/// Writes a cache in the layout of [`save_cache`] back to the device.
fn load_cache(
    c: &mut KvCache,
    window: Option<usize>,
    pos: usize,
    k: &[f32],
    v: &[f32],
) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
    let Some(w) = window else {
        return c.load(0, k, v);
    };
    let n = pos.min(w);
    if n == 0 {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let (slots, kv_dim) = (c.slots(), k.len() / n);
    let device = |x: &[f32]| window_to_slots(x, kv_dim, slots, pos);
    c.load(0, &device(k), &device(v))
}

/// Zeroes a recurrent layer's state; caches simply start over.
pub(super) fn clear_layer(state: &mut LayerState, stream: &Stream) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
    match state {
        LayerState::Attention(_) => Ok(()),
        LayerState::DeltaNet(s) => s.clear(stream),
        LayerState::ShortConv(s) => s.clear(stream),
        LayerState::Mamba2(s) => s.clear(stream),
        LayerState::Parallel(ss) => ss.iter_mut().try_for_each(|s| clear_layer(s, stream)),
    }
}

impl CudaModel<'_> {
    /// The host form of `state`, which `model`, the model this one was
    /// uploaded from, runs on the CPU. It holds exactly the device values,
    /// so [`CudaModel::device_state`] gives the same state back.
    pub fn host_state(&self, model: &Model, state: &CudaState) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<State> {
        assert!(state.checkpoint.is_none(), "host copy inside a checkpoint");
        let mut host = model.new_state();
        host.pos = state.pos;
        host.layers[..self.front].clone_from_slice(&state.work.front);
        for ((layer, ls), hs) in self
            .layer_states(&state.work)
            .zip(&mut host.layers[self.front..])
        {
            let bufs = layer.mixer.save(ls, state.pos)?;
            for (dst, src) in hs.buffers_mut().into_iter().zip(bufs) {
                *dst = src;
            }
        }
        host.marks = state.marks.clone();
        Ok(host)
    }

    /// A new device state holding `state`, the host form of one this model
    /// ran, as [`CudaModel::host_state`] or the warm cache give it.
    pub fn device_state(&self, state: &State) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<CudaState> {
        let mut dev = self.new_state()?;
        self.load_state(&mut dev, state)?;
        Ok(dev)
    }

    /// [`CudaModel::device_state`] into the buffers of `dev`, a state of
    /// this model whose contents it replaces, which saves allocating them.
    pub fn load_state(&self, dev: &mut CudaState, state: &State) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
        if state.pos == 0 {
            return self.reset_state(dev);
        }
        dev.pos = state.pos;
        dev.checkpoint = None;
        dev.work.front = state.layers[..self.front].to_vec();
        for ((_, layer, ls), hs) in self
            .device_layers(&mut dev.work)
            .zip(&state.layers[self.front..])
        {
            layer.mixer.load(ls, state.pos, &hs.buffers())?;
        }
        dev.marks = state.marks.clone();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Empties `dev`, a state of this model, for a new sequence in the same
    /// buffers: recurrent layers are zeroed on the device, the layers on the
    /// host start afresh, caches simply start over.
    pub fn reset_state(&self, dev: &mut CudaState) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
        if dev.pos == 0 && dev.checkpoint.is_none() {
            return Ok(());
        }
        dev.pos = 0;
        dev.checkpoint = None;
        dev.marks.clear();

        self.device_layers(&mut dev.work)
            .try_for_each(|(gpu, _, s)| clear_layer(s, &gpu.stream))
    }

}

impl VulkanModel<'_> {
    /// The host form of `state`, which `model`, the model this one was
    /// uploaded from, runs on the CPU. It holds exactly the device values,
    /// so [`VulkanModel::device_state`] gives the same state back.
    pub fn host_state(&self, model: &Model, state: &VulkanState) -> R<State> {
        assert!(state.checkpoint.is_none(), "host copy inside a checkpoint");
        let mut host = model.new_state();
        host.pos = state.pos;
        let layers = self.layers.iter().zip(&state.layers).zip(&mut host.layers);
        for ((layer, s), hs) in layers {
            for (dst, src) in hs.buffers_mut().into_iter().zip(layer.save(s, state.pos)?) {
                *dst = src;
            }
        }
        host.marks = state.marks.clone();
        Ok(host)
    }

    /// A new device state holding `state`, the host form of one this model
    /// ran, as [`VulkanModel::host_state`] or the warm cache give it.
    pub fn device_state(&self, state: &State) -> R<VulkanState> {
        let mut dev = self.new_state()?;
        self.load_state(&mut dev, state)?;
        Ok(dev)
    }

    /// [`VulkanModel::device_state`] into the buffers of `dev`, a state of
    /// this model whose contents it replaces.
    pub fn load_state(&self, dev: &mut VulkanState, state: &State) -> R<()> {
        dev.pos = state.pos;
        dev.checkpoint = None;
        let layers = self.layers.iter().zip(&mut dev.layers).zip(&state.layers);
        for ((layer, s), hs) in layers {
            layer.load(s, state.pos, &hs.buffers())?;
        }
        dev.marks = state.marks.clone();
        Ok(())
    }

    /// Keeps host copies of the layers a truncation cannot cut back in
    /// place, as [`Model::mark`] does.
    fn mark(&self, model: &Model, state: &mut VulkanState) -> R<()> {
        if state.marks.last().is_some_and(|m| m.pos == state.pos) {
            return Ok(());
        }
        let mut layers = Vec::with_capacity(self.layers.len());
        let all = self.layers.iter().zip(&state.layers).zip(&model.layers);
        for ((layer, s), host) in all {
            layers.push(match host.mixer.needs_mark() {
                true => {
                    let mut hs = host.mixer.new_state();
                    for (dst, src) in hs.buffers_mut().into_iter().zip(layer.save(s, state.pos)?) {
                        *dst = src;
                    }
                    Some(hs)
                }
                false => None,
            });
        }
        state.marks.push(Mark {
            pos: state.pos,
            layers,
        });
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// one vector, rather than one that generates text.
fn is_embedding_model(path: &Path) -> Result<bool> {
    let file = ModelFile::open(path)?;
    let header = file.source().header();
    let encoder = header
        .architecture()
        .is_some_and(kinetic_models::is_encoder);
    Ok(encoder || header.arch_key("pooling_type").is_some())
}

/// Reads the model file once in the background so the first answer does not
/// wait for the weights to come off the disk, when it fits easily in memory.
fn read_ahead(path: &Path) {
    let size = std::fs::metadata(path).map_or(u64::MAX, |m| m.len());
    if size > system::machine().ram_available / 2 {
        return;
    }
    let path = path.to_path_buf();
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        use std::io::Read;
        let Ok(mut file) = std::fs::File::open(&path) else {
            return;
        };
        let mut buffer = vec![0u8; 16 << 20];
        while matches!(file.read(&mut buffer), Ok(n) if n > 0) {}
    });
}

#[test]
fn q8_0_cache_stays_close_to_f16() {
    let Some(gpu) = large_batch_gpu() else { return };
    for shape in [
        attention_shape(256, None, true),
        attention_shape(64, Some(40), false),
    ] {
        let exact = attention_outputs(&gpu, shape, [KvType::F16; 2], false, false);
        for types in [
            [KvType::Q8_0; 2],
            [KvType::Q8_0, KvType::F16],
            [KvType::F16, KvType::Q8_0],
        ] {
            let steps = attention_outputs(&gpu, shape, types, false, false);
            assert_close(&format!("{types:?} {shape:?}"), &steps, &exact, 2e-2);
            // the flash kernel widens q8_0 to f16 tiles
            let batched = attention_outputs(&gpu, shape, types, true, false);
            assert_close(
                &format!("flash {types:?} {shape:?}"),
                &batched,
                &steps,
                2e-3,
            );
        }
    }
}

#[test]
fn q8_0_cache_saves_and_loads_unchanged() {
    let Some(gpu) = gpu() else { return };
    let shape = attention_shape(128, None, false);
    let slots = 8;
    let len = slots * shape.n_head_kv * shape.head_dim;
    let mut rng = Lcg(3);
    let (k, v) = (random(&mut rng, len, 3.0), random(&mut rng, len, 0.5));
    let mut cache =
        KvCache::with_types(&gpu.ctx, &shape, slots, KvType::Q8_0, KvType::Q8_0).unwrap();
    cache.load(0, &k, &v).unwrap();
    let (k1, v1) = cache.save(0..slots).unwrap();
    assert_close("q8_0 keys", &k1, &k, 1e-2);
    cache.load(0, &k1, &v1).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(cache.save(0..slots).unwrap(), (k1, v1));
}

The q8_0 save/load test asserts idempotence after one round trip, not that original f32 maps exactly. Warm cache with q8_0: `host_state` saves q8_0 to f32, then `load_state` re-quantizes. The test `q8_0_cache_saves_and_loads_unchanged` loads random f32, saves (dequantizes), loads that, saves again, and asserts the two saves equal. It doesn't assert the first save equals the original (it can't, quantization). For warm exactness, the state after a run is already q8_0; `save` dequantizes to f32; `load` re-quantizes. If the dequantized values re-quantize to the same q8_0 codes, exact. The test suggests idempotence after one round trip, which is exactly what's needed: state q8_0 -> save f32 -> load q8_0 should be identical. The test loads random f32 (quantizes), saves (dequantizes), loads (re-quantizes), saves, asserts equal. So yes, round-trip is idempotent. Warm exactness holds. Good. But it's still worth a test with actual warm + q8_0; not present. We can mention as a verification gap, not a bug.

Now, let's inspect `CudaState` and `VulkanState` memory: `Work::new` allocates per-layer caches and scratch. `state_bytes` includes work + layers. The KV cache is inside `LayerState::Attention(KvCache)`, allocated with `capacity = context`, `rows = MAX_BATCH` (or `PROMPT_BATCH` for Vulkan). So per-slot KV = full context * kv_dim * 2 bytes (f16) or q8_0 ~1.06 bytes/value. No dynamic growth; full context reserved. This is a key improvement: allocate KV lazily by pages/blocks, not full context; or use a shared pool across slots. This directly improves `--parallel` and long-context memory.

Let's inspect `CudaModel::load` context and `Placement` to see if context is capped. Not necessary.

Now, what improvements should we recommend? Let's structure:

### 1. Current state (facts)
- CPU:
  - `KvCache` = `Vec<f32>` K and V, contiguous per layer/sequence; optional ring for sliding window; journal for speculative rollback; `SharedKv` lend/borrow copies; `State` per sequence; warm cache stores host states.
  - F32 = 4 bytes/value; `state_bytes` computes 2 * n_head_kv * head_dim * min(len, window) * 4.
- CUDA:
  - `KvCache` with `KvType::{F16, Q8_0}` per K/V; blocks of 32 for q8_0; contiguous slots per sequence; full `context` allocated at load; ring for window; `copy_kv` for shared layers only f16; `save/load` for warm cache; checkpoint/rollback via position + replay for recurrent layers; `CudaBackend::slot` shares weights and allocates full state per slot.
  - `--cache-type-k/v f16|q8_0`; q8_0 ~half memory, changes outputs.
- Vulkan:
  - `KvCache` f16 only; contiguous slots; full context; ring for window; no q8_0; one backend (no parallel slots); warm cache host states; checkpoint/rollback with replay.
- Server:
  - `Engine.free` pool of backends; one request per backend; `--parallel` creates N backends (CUDA slots, CPU backends; Vulkan ignores).
  - No paged KV, no continuous batching, no prefix sharing between active sequences, no KV eviction except Warm Start LRU at sequence granularity.
  - Warm Start: 1 GiB RAM + 2 GiB disk, exact states, aligned chunks; prefix cache at sequence granularity; disk files `.kwarm`.
- Memory sizing:
  - `state_bytes(context) * slots` for CPU; CUDA `state_bytes` full context; `gpu_context` adjusts context to fit weights + cache; q8_0 share used for estimate.
  - Full-context reservation means a 32k context model with `--parallel 4` can waste huge memory; long context may not fit even if actual sequence is short.

### 2. Limits / risks
- Memory fragmentation / over-reservation: full context per slot, no paging; `--parallel` memory scales linearly; Vulkan no parallel.
- No prefix sharing between concurrent requests: each sequence has its own KV; Warm Start only helps across requests after a completed prompt, not concurrent shared system prompts.
- No page-level eviction/defrag: Warm Start evicts whole states; KV pages cannot be evicted individually; no host/device tiering for KV.
- Quantization asymmetry: CUDA q8_0, Vulkan f16, CPU f32; exactness gates differ; shared KV `copy_kv` f16 only; q8_0 + shared KV unsupported.
- Rollback/speculation: journal/replay is exact but expensive; paged KV must preserve exact rollback and copy-on-write for tree verification. `MAX_BATCH`/`PROMPT_BATCH` constraints.
- Sliding window ring overallocates `w + rows`; with paged KV, eviction can be page-granular.
- Warm cache exactness: sequence-level, stores full state (including recurrent layers), 1 GiB/2 GiB; disk I/O; no partial prefix sharing; q8_0 round-trip should be tested.
- Multi-GPU/sharding: `copy_kv` copies full caches for shared layers; no distributed KV.
- Model families: MLA/DSA, attention sinks, SSM/hybrid need different KV/state layouts; current `MixerState` supports DeltaNet/ShortConv/Mamba2 but not MLA compressed KV. A generic KV abstraction should account for non-attention state.
- `n > 1` / beam search: no copy-on-write; would duplicate KV.
- Concurrency: one request per backend; no token-level batching; KV pool would enable continuous batching.

### 3. Potential improvements (prioritized)
P0:
1. **KV memory accounting and lazy allocation**: allocate KV pages on demand, not full context; cap by actual sequence length; share pool across slots. Quick win: dynamic growth/`context` cap per sequence, `--parallel` memory based on expected lengths. But exactness and performance? Lazy allocation avoids over-reservation.
2. **Paged KV cache**: block table per sequence, page size (e.g., 16/32/64 tokens), physical page pool, free list, refcounts; prefix sharing via page hash; copy-on-write for branches; rollback truncates block table; sliding window evicts pages. This is the big architectural improvement. It enables continuous batching, prefix caching, `n>1`, beam search, multi-turn.
3. **Prefix caching at page level**: share pages for common system prompts across active sequences; hash page content/token prefix; refcount; LRU eviction; avoid full-state Warm Start for active requests. Keep Warm Start for cross-run/disk exact states, but use page sharing for concurrent requests.
4. **KV quantization parity**: add q8_0 to Vulkan; q4_0/q5_1 maybe; FP8; per-layer K/V type; q8_0 + shared KV support; exactness tests; warm cache round-trip with q8_0. CUDA already has q8_0; Vulkan is the gap.
5. **KV layout for GQA/MLA/DSA**: pack K/V heads, support MLA compressed latent KV, DSA indexer cache, attention sinks; separate "state" abstraction for SSM/hybrid. Current `KvCache` is per-head K/V; MLA needs latent cache + rope cache; DSA needs indexer keys. This is model-family-driven.
6. **Memory tiering/offload**: host KV for cold pages, device KV for hot; async copies; pinned memory; unified memory; NVMe? For local inference, host offload can extend context; but latency. Warm Start disk is a coarse version.
7. **KV cache-aware scheduling**: admission control based on KV pages; eviction; fairness; chunked prefill; continuous batching; prefix-aware routing. This ties to runtime.
8. **Exactness/verification**: bit-exact rollback, batch-invariance, warm/cold equality, q8_0 tolerance, long-context needle, shared-prefix equality. Add a KV conformance suite.
9. **Observability**: KV bytes used/free, pages, hit rate, evictions, fragmentation, per-request KV footprint, TTFT vs KV hit.
10. **Multi-GPU**: shard KV by layer/head; avoid `copy_kv` full copies; page ownership; P2P.

Prioritization:
- P0: measure current KV footprint and hit rates; add q8_0 Vulkan; page-level prefix sharing? The user asks "améliorations potentielles" — we can present a roadmap.
- The biggest win for performance: paged KV + prefix sharing + continuous batching. But the biggest immediate gap on Vulkan is q8_0 and parallel slots. The docs earlier said KV f16 only; we should correct.
- For single-user local inference, full-context reservation may be acceptable; for server/concurrency, paged KV is essential.
- The measured gaps: Vulkan prefill 4.4x, MoE 3.3-5.4x; KV cache is not the primary cause of prefill gap (GEMM is). But KV affects long-context, concurrency, TTFT, memory. Need to be clear: KV improvements won't fix the 4.4x prefill gap; they unlock concurrency/long context and reduce memory. The user asks specifically about KV; we should not overstate its impact on prefill.
- For MoE decode, KV is less of a bottleneck than expert memory reads. But KV quantization frees memory for experts, indirectly helping MoE.
- For long context, KV size dominates; q8_0 halves it; paging/prefix sharing helps multi-turn.

    let weights = fit::Weights::of(header);
    // experts leave the GPU by design, --gpu-layers asked for a split and
    // --gpus for several GPUs, which this does not add up
    if !gpu || runtime.gpu_layers.is_some() || runtime.gpus.len() > 1 || weights.has_experts() {
        return wanted;
    }
    let Some(free) = system::cuda_free() else {
        return wanted;
    };
    // state_bytes counts f32; the GPU keeps attention caches in --cache-type-*
    let share = |t: CacheType| match t {
        CacheType::F16 => 0.5,
        CacheType::Q8_0 => 34.0 / 128.0,
    };
    let share = (share(runtime.cache_type_k) + share(runtime.cache_type_v)) / 2.0;
    let fixed = model.state_bytes(0) as u64;
    let cache = |n| fixed + ((model.state_bytes(n) as u64 - fixed) as f64 * share) as u64;
    match fit::gpu_context(wanted, free, weights.total(), cache) {
        Some(n) => {
            eprintln!(
                "kinetic: context {}k to fit the GPU; -c to change",
                n / 1024
            );
            n
        }
        None => wanted,
    }

const CPU: &str = "the CPU";

/// Most requests answered at once when the user does not say.
const MAX_DEFAULT_SLOTS: usize = 4;

/// As many sequences of `context` tokens as half the free memory holds, at
/// least one and at most [`MAX_DEFAULT_SLOTS`].
fn default_slots(model: &Model, context: usize) -> usize {
    let per = model.state_bytes(context).max(1) as u64;
    kinetic_models::memory::available().map_or(1, |free| {
        ((free / 2 / per) as usize).clamp(1, MAX_DEFAULT_SLOTS)
    })
}

`-ctv`) store keys and values in blocks of 32 int8 values with one f16
scale, 34 bytes where f16 takes 64. Every token stays in the cache, but its
keys and values are rounded, so answers differ from the f16 cache's: close
in quality, not identical, and never what the exactness checks compare
against. It is off by default. The CPU and Vulkan paths ignore it.

**Warm Start keeps prompt states** in up to 1 GiB of RAM and 2 GiB on disk,
under `--cache-dir` (by default `kinetic/warm` in `%LOCALAPPDATA%` on
Windows and `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` or `~/.cache` on Linux and macOS). `--no-prompt-cache`
turns it off.

`kinetic bench` reports the peak memory of a run.

## Mixture-of-experts offload

A mixture-of-experts model that does not fit in GPU memory still runs on the
GPU with `--device auto` or `cuda`. Kinetic puts the attention layers, the
shared weights and the cache on the GPU, gives the remaining free memory to
a cache of experts, and leaves the other experts in the memory-mapped file.
Each layer then runs the experts it picks where that is cheapest at the
moment: from the GPU cache, on the CPU, or copied over. See
[Flywheel](how-it-is-fast.md#flywheel) for how it decides.

For this to be fast, the whole file should fit in system RAM next to your
other programs. Kinetic reads the experts into memory at load time when they
fit with 3 GiB to spare, and otherwise lets the first tokens read them as
needed.

When every expert fits on the GPU, there is no offload: routing runs on the
GPU too.

- **More on Vulkan**: more architectures, speculative decoding, Warm Start
  and layer splits.
- **Several GPUs** for mixture-of-experts models, Gemma 4 E2B/E4B and
  shared passes; dense models already spread over them with `--gpus`.

See the [roadmap](roadmap.md).
The chosen tokens, their order and their scores are those of the full layer,
bit for bit, because every exact score comes from the layer's own kernel.
Shortlist serves greedy decoding, top-k sampling and draft verification. It
works on the CPU, for output layers stored as Q6_K or Q8_0.

## Flywheel

A mixture-of-experts (MoE) model has many expert feed-forward blocks per
layer and uses only a few of them for each token: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B uses about
3 billion of its 35 billion parameters per token. The model is large, but the
work per token is small, if the right experts are at hand.

```text
GPU memory    [attention, shared weights, KV cache][ expert cache: the experts in use ]
system RAM    [ every expert, memory-mapped from the model file                     ]

per layer     the router picks a few experts
              in the cache   -> run on the GPU
              not in cache   -> run on the CPU, or copy to the GPU, whichever is cheaper now
              next layer     -> likely experts prefetched while this one runs
```

Flywheel gives the experts all the GPU memory left after the rest of the
model, one sequence's state and a reserve. It measures how fast the CPU runs
an expert and how fast one copies to the GPU, keeps adjusting for other
programs that slow the CPU down, and splits the work accordingly. When every
expert fits, routing happens on the GPU and each one-token step runs as one
recorded CUDA graph. Expert offloading itself is known (for example Eliseev
and Mazur, 2023, and llama.cpp's `--override-tensor`); Flywheel makes the
placement automatic.

See [Devices and offload](devices.md) for what runs where.

Le cache KV est un levier direct de mémoire et de vitesse en contexte long. Ajouter
`q4_0`, `q4_1`, `iq4_nl`, `q5_0`, `q5_1`, `bf16` et `f32` dans
`kinetic-hip/src/attention.rs`, `kinetic-vulkan/src/attention.rs`, le chemin CPU et
`kinetic-cuda/src/attention.rs` (`KvType`). Sur la RX 9070 XT, q8_0 est le premier
gain utile : il double la capacité de contexte sans changer les noyaux de calcul.

to `-c` tokens, 32768 by default (less if the model was trained on less;

reserved at load time, so a model that does not fit with the default

in quality, not identical, and never what the exactness checks compare
against. It is off by default. The CPU and Vulkan paths ignore it.

use kinetic_quant::Matrix;
use kinetic_vulkan::{
    AttentionGate, AttentionShape, Commands, DeviceBuffer, DeviceMatrix, KvCache, Out, QkvConsts,
    Rows,
};

use super::layer::{unsupported, R};
use super::rope::RopeTables;
use super::work::{Needs, Work};
use super::Gpu;
use crate::blocks::{Attention, Gate, RopeLayout};
use crate::LoadError;

/// Attention on the device; see [`Attention`].
pub(super) struct VulkanAttention {
    pub shape: AttentionShape,
    q: DeviceMatrix,
    k: DeviceMatrix,
    v: DeviceMatrix,
    o: DeviceMatrix,
    /// One gate value per head, when the layer has them.
    head_gate: Option<DeviceMatrix>,
    /// Query and key norms and the projection biases, at the offsets below.
    consts: DeviceBuffer<f32>,
    q_norm: Option<usize>,
    k_norm: Option<usize>,
    bias: Option<usize>,
    /// The batch table word where this layer's rotary angles start.
    rope_table: usize,
}

impl VulkanAttention {
    pub fn upload(gpu: &Gpu, a: &Attention, ropes: &mut RopeTables) -> Result<Self, LoadError> {
        let gate = match a.gate {
            Gate::Interleaved => AttentionGate::PerValue,
            Gate::PerHead(_) => AttentionGate::PerHead,
            Gate::None => AttentionGate::None,
        };
        let v_norm = match &a.v_norm {
            None => false,
            Some(w) if w.iter().all(|&w| w == 1.0) => true,
            Some(_) => return Err(unsupported("weighted value norms")),
        };
        let per_head = |n: &Option<Vec<f32>>| n.as_ref().is_none_or(|w| w.len() == a.head_dim);
        if !per_head(&a.q_norm) || !per_head(&a.k_norm) {
            return Err(unsupported("query and key norms across heads"));
        }
        let shape = AttentionShape {
            n_head: a.n_head,
            n_head_kv: a.n_head_kv,
            head_dim: a.head_dim,
            rope_dims: a.rope.dims,
            rope_adjacent: a.rope.layout == RopeLayout::Adjacent,
            norm_after_rope: a.norm_after_rope,
            gate,
            window: a.window,
            scale: a.scale.unwrap_or(1.0 / (a.head_dim as f32).sqrt()),
            eps: a.eps,
            v_norm,
        };
        if a.q.rows != a.n_head * shape.q_head_len() || a.k.rows != shape.kv_dim() {
            return Err(LoadError(format!(
                "attention projections of {} and {} rows do not fit {shape:?}",
                a.q.rows, a.k.rows
            )));
        }

        let mut consts = Vec::new();
        let mut push = |v: &[f32]| {
            let at = consts.len();
            consts.extend_from_slice(v);
            at
        };
        let q_norm = a.q_norm.as_deref().map(&mut push);
        let k_norm = a.k_norm.as_deref().map(&mut push);
        let bias = (a.q_bias.is_some() || a.k_bias.is_some() || a.v_bias.is_some()).then(|| {
            let part = |b: &Option<Vec<f32>>, len: usize| b.clone().unwrap_or(vec![0.0; len]);
            let mut all = part(&a.q_bias, a.q.rows);
            all.extend(part(&a.k_bias, a.k.rows));
            all.extend(part(&a.v_bias, a.v.rows));
            push(&all)
        });
        if consts.is_empty() {
            consts.push(0.0);
        }
        let matrix = |m: &Matrix| gpu.matrix(m);
        Ok(VulkanAttention {
            q: matrix(&a.q)?,
            k: matrix(&a.k)?,
            v: matrix(&a.v)?,
            o: matrix(&a.o)?,
            head_gate: match &a.gate {
                Gate::PerHead(g) => Some(matrix(g)?),
                Gate::Interleaved | Gate::None => None,
            },
            consts: gpu.vector(&consts)?,
            q_norm,
            k_norm,
            bias,
            rope_table: ropes.table(&a.rope)?,
            shape,
        })
    }

    pub fn size_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        [&self.q, &self.k, &self.v, &self.o]
            .into_iter()
            .chain(&self.head_gate)
            .map(DeviceMatrix::size_bytes)
            .sum()
    }

    pub fn needs(&self) -> Needs {
        let s = &self.shape;
        Needs {
            proj: s.qkv_len(),
            width: s.n_head * s.head_dim,
            rec: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Reads `w.h` and leaves the projected output in `w.y`.
    pub fn record(&self, gpu: &Gpu, w: &Work, cache: &KvCache, c: &mut Commands) -> R {
        let (k, s) = (&gpu.kernels, &self.shape);
        let stride = s.qkv_len();
        let q_len = s.n_head * s.q_head_len();
        let projections = [
            (&self.q, 0),
            (&self.k, q_len),
            (&self.v, q_len + s.kv_dim()),
        ];
        let gates = self.head_gate.iter().map(|g| (g, s.gate_at()));
        // The projections write disjoint columns of each row.
        c.independent(|c| {
            for (m, offset) in projections.into_iter().chain(gates) {
                let out = Out { stride, offset };
                k.gemv_rows(m, &w.h, &w.proj, out, Rows::Tokens, &w.batch, c)?;
            }
            Ok(())
        })?;

/// How a [`KvCache`] stores keys or values.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum KvType {
    /// f16 values.
    #[default]
    F16,
    /// q8_0: blocks of 32 int8 values times an f16 scale, 34 bytes where f16
    /// takes 64. Attention then reads rounded values, so outputs change.
    Q8_0,
}

/// Values per q8_0 block; head sizes are multiples of it.
const Q8_BLOCK: usize = 32;

enum Store {
    F16(DeviceBuffer<u16>),
    Q8_0 {
        quants: DeviceBuffer<i8>,
        scales: DeviceBuffer<u16>,
    },
}

impl Store {
    fn new(ctx: &Rc<Context>, ty: KvType, len: usize) -> Result<Store> {
        Ok(match ty {
            KvType::F16 => Store::F16(DeviceBuffer::new(ctx, len)?),
            KvType::Q8_0 => Store::Q8_0 {
                quants: DeviceBuffer::new(ctx, len)?,
                scales: DeviceBuffer::new(ctx, len / Q8_BLOCK)?,
            },
        })
    }

    /// The values and the scales, 0 for f16.
    fn ptrs(&self) -> (u64, u64) {
        match self {
            Store::F16(v) => (v.device_ptr(), 0),
            Store::Q8_0 { quants, scales } => (quants.device_ptr(), scales.device_ptr()),
        }
    }

    fn size_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        match self {
            Store::F16(v) => 2 * v.len(),
            Store::Q8_0 { quants, scales } => quants.len() + 2 * scales.len(),
        }
    }

    /// Values `start..start + out.len()`; `start` is a multiple of 32.
    fn save(&self, start: usize, out: &mut [f32]) -> Result<()> {
        match self {
            Store::F16(v) => {
                let mut bits = vec![0; out.len()];
                v.copy_range_to(start, &mut bits)?;
                for (o, b) in out.iter_mut().zip(bits) {
                    *o = f16::from_bits(b).to_f32();
                }
            }
            Store::Q8_0 { quants, scales } => {
                let mut q = vec![0; out.len()];
                let mut d = vec![0; out.len() / Q8_BLOCK];
                quants.copy_range_to(start, &mut q)?;
                scales.copy_range_to(start / Q8_BLOCK, &mut d)?;
                for ((out, q), d) in out.chunks_mut(Q8_BLOCK).zip(q.chunks(Q8_BLOCK)).zip(d) {
                    let d = f16::from_bits(d).to_f32();
                    for (o, &q) in out.iter_mut().zip(q) {
                        *o = d * f32::from(q);
                    }
                }
            }
        }
pub struct KvCache {
    k: Store,
    v: Store,
    slots: usize,
    kv_dim: usize,
}

impl KvCache {
    /// An f16 cache of `slots` positions for layers of `shape`. A windowed
    /// cache needs more slots than its window by the most tokens that may be
    /// run and then rolled back, since those overwrite the oldest entries.
    pub fn new(ctx: &Rc<Context>, shape: &AttentionShape, slots: usize) -> Result<KvCache> {
        KvCache::with_types(ctx, shape, slots, KvType::F16, KvType::F16)
    }

    /// [`KvCache::new`] with keys stored as `k` and values as `v`.
    pub fn with_types(
        ctx: &Rc<Context>,
        shape: &AttentionShape,
        slots: usize,
        k: KvType,
        v: KvType,
    ) -> Result<KvCache> {
        shape.check()?;
        if shape.window.is_some_and(|w| slots <= w) || u32::try_from(slots).is_err() {
            return Err(Error::Shape(format!(
                "{slots} cache slots for a window of {:?}",
                shape.window
            )));
        }
        let len = slots * shape.kv_dim();
        Ok(KvCache {
            k: Store::new(ctx, k, len)?,
            v: Store::new(ctx, v, len)?,
            slots,
            kv_dim: shape.kv_dim(),
        })
    }

    pub fn slots(&self) -> usize {
        self.slots
    }

    /// Device bytes held.
    pub fn size_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.k.size_bytes() + self.v.size_bytes()
    }

    /// Copies the keys and values of `slots` to the host.
    pub fn save(&self, slots: Range<usize>) -> Result<(Vec<f32>, Vec<f32>)> {
        let len = slots.len() * self.kv_dim;
        let (mut k, mut v) = (vec![0.0; len], vec![0.0; len]);
        self.k.save(slots.start * self.kv_dim, &mut k)?;
        self.v.save(slots.start * self.kv_dim, &mut v)?;
        Ok((k, v))
    }

    /// Writes keys and values from [`KvCache::save`] at slot `at` on.
    pub fn load(&mut self, at: usize, k: &[f32], v: &[f32]) -> Result<()> {
        self.k.load(at * self.kv_dim, k)?;
        self.v.load(at * self.kv_dim, v)
    }
}

#[cfg(feature = "cuda")]
fn cuda_backend<'a>(
    model: &'a Model<'a>,
    path: &Path,
    runtime: &RuntimeArgs,
    context: usize,
    parallel: Option<usize>,
) -> Option<std::result::Result<Placed<'a>, kinetic_models::LoadError>> {
    let placement = kinetic_models::cuda::Placement {
        gpu_layers: runtime.gpu_layers,
        devices: runtime.gpus.clone(),
        eager: runtime.is_off(Tech::Torque),
        cache_k: runtime.cache_type_k.into(),
        cache_v: runtime.cache_type_v.into(),
        ..kinetic_models::cuda::Placement::default()
    };
    let gpu = match kinetic_server::CudaBackend::with_placement(model, context, placement) {
        Ok(gpu) if runtime.is_off(Tech::Rad1) => gpu.without_drafts(),
        Ok(gpu) => gpu,
        Err(e) => return Some(Err(e)),
    };
    let name = gpu.device().to_owned();
    let mut slots: Vec<Box<dyn Backend + 'a>> = Vec::new();
    for _ in 1..parallel.unwrap_or(MAX_DEFAULT_SLOTS) {
        match gpu.slot() {
            Ok(slot) => slots.push(Box::new(slot)),
            Err(e) if parallel.is_some() => {
                let e = format!("--parallel {}: {e}", slots.len() + 2);
                return Some(Err(kinetic_models::LoadError(e)));
            }
            Err(_) => break,
        }
    }
    let gpu = match warm_cache(model, path, runtime, Some("cuda")) {
        Some(w) => gpu.with_warm(w),
        None => gpu,
    };
    slots.insert(0, Box::new(gpu));
    Some(Ok((slots, name)))
}

    /// Uploads `model` to the first Vulkan device that can run it, for
    /// sequences of up to `context` tokens. Fails when no device is usable
    /// or the model needs something the Vulkan kernels lack.
    pub fn new(model: &'a Model<'a>, context: usize) -> Result<Self, LoadError> {
        let gpu = VulkanModel::load(model, context)?;
        let state = gpu.new_state().map_err(vulkan_error)?;
        // the drafter's cache shares the memory, so a full device fails here
        // and not on the first request
        drop(gpu.new_mtp_state().map_err(vulkan_error)?);
        Ok(VulkanBackend {
            decoder: drafter::decoder(&gpu),
            cached: Some(Sequence {

                tokens: Vec::new(),

            warm: None,

    /// An empty state for a new sequence.
    pub fn new_state(&self) -> kinetic_vulkan::Result<VulkanState> {
        let dev = &self.gpu.device;
        let work = |rows, head_rows| {
            let batch = Batch::new(dev, rows, head_rows, self.context, self.ropes.words())?;
            Work::new(&self.gpu, &self.layers, self.n_embd, batch, self.n_vocab())
        };
        // A prompt pass wants the logits of its last token at most.
        let many = PROMPT_BATCH > MAX_BATCH;
        let prompt_work = match many {
            true => Some(work(PROMPT_BATCH, 1)?),
            false => None,
        };
        let work = work(MAX_BATCH, MAX_BATCH)?;
        let layers = self
            .layers
            .iter()
            .map(|l| l.new_state(dev, self.context, PROMPT_BATCH))
            .collect::<kinetic_vulkan::Result<Vec<_>>>()?;
        let vocab = self.n_vocab();
        let mut all_logits = Commands::new(dev)?;
        all_logits.download(&work.logits, 0, &work.logits_host, 0, MAX_BATCH * vocab)?;
        let replay = match self.layers.iter().any(VulkanLayer::replays) {
            true => Some(self.record_replay(&work, &layers)?),
            false => None,
        };
        Ok(VulkanState {
            pos: 0,
            checkpoint: None,
            step: self.record(&work, &layers, false, false)?,
            step_logits: self.record(&work, &layers, true, false)?,
            step_prompt: self.record(
                prompt_work.as_ref().unwrap_or(&work),
                &layers,
                false,
                many,
            )?,
            step_prompt_logits: self.record(
                prompt_work.as_ref().unwrap_or(&work),
                &layers,
                true,
                many,
            )?,
            all_logits: all_logits.finish()?,
            replay,
            work,
            prompt_work,
            layers,
            marks: Vec::new(),
        })
    }

        }
        Ok(())
    }

#[cfg(feature = "vulkan")]
fn vulkan_backend<'a>(
    model: &'a Model<'a>,
    path: &Path,
    runtime: &RuntimeArgs,
    context: usize,
) -> Option<std::result::Result<Placed<'a>, kinetic_models::LoadError>> {
    Some(
        kinetic_server::VulkanBackend::new(model, context).map(|gpu| {
            let gpu = match runtime.is_off(Tech::Rad1) {
                true => gpu.without_drafts(),
                false => gpu,
            };
            let name = gpu.device().to_owned();
            let gpu = match warm_cache(model, path, runtime, Some("vulkan")) {
                Some(w) => gpu.with_warm(w),
                None => gpu,
            };
            (vec![Box::new(gpu) as Box<dyn Backend>], name)
        }),
    )
}

    /// Uploads the routed experts of the mixture this feed-forward runs.
    fn upload_experts(&mut self, gpu: &Gpu, l: &Layer) -> Result<(), LoadError> {
        match (&mut *self, &l.experts) {
            (VulkanFeed::Moe(m), Some(experts)) | (VulkanFeed::Shared(_, m), Some(experts)) => {

    fn widths(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = usize> + '_ {
        match self {
            VulkanFeed::Dense(f) => [Some(f.gate.rows()), None],
            VulkanFeed::Moe(m) => [None, Some(m.n_ff())],
            VulkanFeed::Shared(f, m) => [Some(f.gate.rows()), Some(m.n_ff())],
        }
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
    }
