//! The generation loop every backend shares: prefill a cached sequence,
//! then decode speculatively under a [`Policy`].

use kinetic_models::speculative::{Decoder, Drafter, Greedy, Policy, Sampler, Target};

use crate::backend::{Job, Timings};
use crate::constrained::Constrained;

/// Prompt tokens per forward pass on the CPU; bounds the activations of
/// long prompts. Prompts are cut at multiples of a backend's chunk, which is
/// also where its warm starts resume, so both run the same batches.
pub const PREFILL_CHUNK: usize = 256;

/// CPU prompt runs give the same bits wherever they are cut on multiples of
/// this many tokens after where they started: delta-net layers run batches
/// of 32 or more in chunks of 16, and fewer token by token.
pub const PREFILL_GRID: usize = 32;

/// A sequence a backend keeps between requests.
pub struct Sequence<S> {
    pub state: S,
    /// Every token `state` has run.
    pub tokens: Vec<u32>,
}

impl<S> Sequence<S> {
    /// Whether `prompt` continues this sequence with at least one new token.
    pub fn continues(&self, prompt: &[u32]) -> bool {
        prompt.len() > self.tokens.len() && prompt.starts_with(&self.tokens)
    }
}

/// A backend that runs a request under any policy; [`generate`] picks the
/// policy the request asks for.
pub trait Run<M: Target> {
    fn run<P: Policy<M>>(
        &mut self,
        prompt: &[u32],
        job: &Job,
        policy: &mut P,
        emit: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u32]) -> bool,
    ) -> Timings;
}

/// Runs `job` on `backend` with greedy choice, seeded sampling or a
/// grammar, as the job asks.
pub fn generate<M: Target, B: Run<M>>(
    backend: &mut B,
    prompt: &[u32],
    job: &Job,
    emit: &mut dyn FnMut(&[u32]) -> bool,
) -> Timings {
    assert!(!prompt.is_empty(), "empty prompt");
    let greedy = job.sampling.is_greedy() && job.logprobs.is_none();
    let sampler = || {
        let sampler = Sampler::new(job.sampling.clone());
        match job.logprobs {
            Some(log) => sampler.with_logprobs(log.clone()),
            None => sampler,
        }
    };
    if let Some((grammar, vocab)) = job.grammar {
        let mut policy = Constrained::new(grammar, vocab, prompt.len(), (!greedy).then(sampler));
        return backend.run(prompt, job, &mut policy, emit);
    }
    if greedy {
        backend.run(prompt, job, &mut Greedy, emit)
    } else {
        backend.run(prompt, job, &mut sampler(), emit)
    }
}

/// Runs the tokens of `prompt` that `seq` has not run in chunks of `chunk`,
/// the leading ones without choosing and the last through `policy`, which
/// chooses the token after the prompt.
pub fn extend<M: Target, P: Policy<M>, D: Drafter<M>>(
    model: &M,
    decoder: &mut Decoder<D>,
    policy: &mut P,
    seq: &mut Sequence<M::State>,
    prompt: &[u32],
    chunk: usize,
) {
    let start = seq.tokens.len();
    let last = start + (prompt.len() - start - 1) / chunk * chunk;
    for chunk in prompt[start..last].chunks(chunk) {
        decoder.feed(model, &mut seq.state, chunk);
    }
    seq.tokens.extend_from_slice(&prompt[start..]);
    decoder.prefill(model, policy, &mut seq.state, &seq.tokens, last);

    pub fn forward(
        &self,
        gpu: &Gpu,
        s: &mut Scratch,
        cache: &mut KvCache,
        batch: &Batch,
    ) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {

    /// Queues the projections of the first `n` rows of `s.h` into `s.proj`.
    pub fn project(&self, gpu: &Gpu, s: &mut Scratch, n: usize) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
        let (k, stream) = (&gpu.kernels, &gpu.stream);
        let [q, keys, values, gates] = &mut s.proj;
        let x = match &self.folding {
            Some(f) => f.fold(gpu, &s.h, &mut s.folded, n)?,
            None => &s.h,
        };
        gpu.fork()?;
        let side = &gpu.side;
        if let (Some(km), Some(vm)) = (&self.k, &self.v) {
            k.gemv_rows(km, km.rows(), x, 0..n, keys, side)?;
            k.gemv_rows(vm, vm.rows(), x, 0..n, values, side)?;
        }
        if let Some(g) = &self.head_gate {
            k.gemv_rows(g, g.rows(), x, 0..n, gates, side)?;
        }
        k.gemv_rows(&self.q, self.q.rows(), x, 0..n, q, stream)?;
        gpu.join()
    }

/// A batch, its scratch and the per-layer state of one sequence.
pub(super) struct Work {
    pub batch: Batch,
    pub scratch: Scratch,
    pub layers: Vec<LayerState>,
    /// Buffers for routed experts and for passes, in a mixture-of-experts
    /// model.
    pub experts: Option<ExpertWork>,
    pub pass: Option<PassRows>,
    /// The states of the layers that run on the host.
    pub front: Vec<MixerState>,
    /// The batch, scratch and layer states of each shard, on its device.
    pub shards: Vec<Work>,
}

/// A batch and scratch for full prefill batches, lent to whichever state
/// runs one, so that states keep buffers for [`MAX_BATCH`] rows only.
pub(super) struct Spare {
    batch: Batch,
    scratch: Scratch,
    /// Those of each shard.
    shards: Vec<Spare>,
}

impl Spare {
    pub fn new(work: Work) -> Spare {
        Spare {
            batch: work.batch,
            scratch: work.scratch,
            shards: work.shards.into_iter().map(Spare::new).collect(),
        }
    }

    /// Trades these buffers for `work`'s; a second call trades them back.
    pub fn swap(&mut self, work: &mut Work) {
        std::mem::swap(&mut self.batch, &mut work.batch);

    /// Device bytes held, over every device.
    pub fn size_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        self.own_bytes() + self.shards.iter().map(Work::size_bytes).sum::<usize>()
    }

    /// Device bytes held on this work's own device.
    fn own_bytes(&self) -> usize {
        let s = &self.scratch;
        let input = |i: &GemvInput| i.capacity() * i.width() * 6;
        let buffers = s.x.len()
            + s.y.len()
            + s.sum.len()
            + s.scratch.len()
            + s.logits.len()
            + s.per_layer.len()
            + s.per_layer_tokens.len();
        let proj: usize = s.proj.iter().map(DeviceBuffer::len).sum();
        let inputs: usize = s
            .mixed
            .iter()
            .chain(&s.ffn)
            .chain(&s.folded)
            .chain(&s.joined)
            .chain([&s.h])
            .map(input)
            .sum();
        let layers: usize = self.layers.iter().map(LayerState::size_bytes).sum();
        let experts = self.experts.as_ref().map_or(0, ExpertWork::size_bytes)
            + self.pass.as_ref().map_or(0, PassRows::size_bytes);
        4 * (buffers + proj) + inputs + layers + experts
    }
}

_Thinking:_

Good. So CUDA `state_bytes` includes layer KV caches. Vulkan `state_bytes` includes layers too.

Now, key KV facts:

**CPU path:**
- `KvCache` stores `k: Vec<f32>`, `v: Vec<f32>`, one contiguous vector per layer, full context, f32.
- Windowed caches use ring buffer with `w` slots; `store` overwrites at `pos % w`, journal keeps old values for rollback.
- Shared KV: lending layer stores the batch's K/V in `lent`, borrowing layer uses it without own cache.
- `state_bytes` counts 2 * n_head_kv * head_dim * min(window, len) * 4 bytes. F32, no quantization.
- Checkpoint/rollback journal to undo speculative tokens; exact.

**CUDA path:**
- `KvCache` stores K and V as `Store::F16` or `Store::Q8_0`; Q8_0 = int8 blocks of 32 + f16 scale (34 bytes/32 values vs 64 for f16).
- `KvType` only F16/Q8_0; no q4/q5/bf16/f32.
- Q8_0 is opt-in via `--cache-type-k/v`; CPU/Vulkan ignore it.
- Q8_0 supported in prefill and flash attention (flash widens q8_0 to f16 tiles); tests assert closeness 2e-2.
- `copy_kv` for shared KV only supports F16, so shared-KV models (Gemma 4?) can't use Q8_0.
- Q8_0 save/load to host dequantizes to f32 and re-quantizes; test `q8_0_cache_saves_and_loads_unchanged` tolerance 1e-2.
- Caches allocated per layer, per sequence, full `context` slots (+ window extra). Contiguous, no paging.
- `Placement.cache_k/cache_v` set at load; `Gpu.cache` used by `new_cache`.
- `state_bytes` accounts actual bytes via `LayerState::size_bytes`, so memory math is accurate.
- `default_slots` for CPU only; CUDA slots created until memory full, max `MAX_DEFAULT_SLOTS=4`, `SLOT_RESERVE=256 MiB`.
- CUDA server supports multiple slots (one backend per slot), shared model via Arc, one seat at a time.

**Vulkan path:**
- `KvCache` K/V as `DeviceBuffer<u32>` f16, full context or ring for window, plus `rows` extra for rollback.
- No quantized KV at all; `--cache-type-k/v` ignored.
- One backend only (no `slot()`), so Vulkan server is effectively single-sequence; `--parallel` doesn't create Vulkan slots.
- KV allocated at load for full context (`positions = self.context`), plus `PROMPT_BATCH` extra for windowed? `KvCache::new(dev, shape, positions, rows)` with rows=PROMPT_BATCH; slots = window + rows min positions. For non-window, positions.

fn build<'a>(l: &Loader<'a>, b: &Basics) -> Result<Stack<'a>, LoadError> {

    let n_layer = l.usize("block_count")?;
    let n_head = l.usize("attention.head_count")?;
    // Full-attention layers keep a single key-value head per group, so the
    // count is either one number or one per layer.
    let n_head_kv = per_layer(l, "attention.head_count_kv", n_layer)?;
    if n_head_kv.iter().any(|&kv| kv == 0 || !n_head.is_multiple_of(kv)) {
        return Err(LoadError("heads do not split into groups".into()));

impl CudaAttention {
    pub fn upload(gpu: &Gpu, a: &Attention) -> Result<CudaAttention, LoadError> {
        let v_norm = match &a.v_norm {
            None => false,
            Some(w) if w.iter().all(|&w| w == 1.0) => true,
            Some(_) => {
                return Err(LoadError(
                    "weighted value norms are not supported on CUDA yet".into(),
                ))
            }
        };
        let own_kv = !matches!(a.shared_kv, SharedKv::Borrows(_));
        let shape = AttentionShape {
            n_head: a.n_head,
            n_head_kv: a.n_head_kv,
            head_dim: a.head_dim,
            rope_dims: a.rope.dims,
            rope_base: a.rope.base,
            rope_adjacent: a.rope.layout == RopeLayout::Adjacent,
            rope_mscale: a.rope.mscale,
            norm_after_rope: a.norm_after_rope,
            scale: a.scale.unwrap_or(1.0 / (a.head_dim as f32).sqrt()),
            eps: a.eps,
            window: a.window,
            interleaved_gate: matches!(a.gate, Gate::Interleaved),
            v_norm,
        };
        let matrix = |m| gpu.matrix(m).map_err(cuda_error);
        let vector = |v: &Option<Vec<f32>>| {
            v.as_deref()
                .map(|v| gpu.vector(v))
                .transpose()
                .map_err(cuda_error)
        };
        Ok(CudaAttention {
            shape,
            q: matrix(&a.q)?,
            k: own_kv.then(|| matrix(&a.k)).transpose()?,
            v: own_kv.then(|| matrix(&a.v)).transpose()?,
            o: matrix(&a.o)?,
            (CudaMixer::Parallel(ms), LayerState::Parallel(ss)) => ms
                .iter()
                .zip(ss)
                .try_for_each(|(m, s)| m.replay(gpu, s, keep)),
            _ => Ok(()),
        }
    }
}

/// Before layer `to` runs on `batch`: copies into its cache the keys and
/// values layer `from` stored for the batch.
// shortcut: each borrowing layer keeps a full copy of the lender's cache, as
// the host states do; attending over the lender's own would save the memory
pub(super) fn copy_lent(
    gpu: &Gpu,
    states: &mut [LayerState],
    from: usize,
    to: usize,
    batch: &Batch,
) -> kinetic_cuda::Result<()> {
    let (done, rest) = states.split_at_mut(to);
    match (&done[from], &mut rest[0]) {
        (LayerState::Attention(src), LayerState::Attention(dst)) => {
            gpu.kernels.copy_kv(src, dst, batch, &gpu.stream)
        }
        _ => unreachable!("keys are lent between attention layers"),
    }
}

//! Passes that several sequences share.
//!
//! Every sequence that runs at once calls [`Convoy::run`] from its own
//! thread with the work of its next pass. The calls gather until every
//! sequence holding a [`Seat`] has one waiting, or until the first has
//! waited [`GATHER`], and then the last caller runs all of them as one pass
//! over the weights while the others wait for their results. A sequence
//! joins by taking a seat and leaves by dropping it, so requests come and
//! go between passes.
//!
//! A convoy can also hold a device that only one thread may drive at a
//! time. A seat then holds the device too, except while its sequence waits
//! for a pass or steps [`Seat::away`], so seated threads take turns on it
//! and the one that starts a pass drives it for everyone.

use std::panic::{self, AssertUnwindSafe};
use std::sync::{Condvar, Mutex, MutexGuard, PoisonError};
use std::thread::{self, ThreadId};
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

/// Longest a pass waits for seated sequences that are busy elsewhere, such
/// as one writing to a slow client.
const GATHER: Duration = Duration::from_millis(5);

/// Gathers the work of concurrent callers into shared passes.
pub(crate) struct Convoy<J, R> {
    queue: Mutex<Queue<J, R>>,
    turn: Condvar,
    /// Whether seats and passes hold the device.
    device: bool,
}

struct Queue<J, R> {
    seats: usize,
    next: u64,
    waiting: Vec<(u64, J)>,
    /// When the oldest call in `waiting` began to wait for a pass.
    since: Option<Instant>,
    /// Results not yet collected; `None` for jobs of a pass that panicked.
    done: Vec<(u64, Option<R>)>,
    running: bool,
    /// The thread driving the device.
    holder: Option<ThreadId>,
}

/// A sequence's place in the passes of a model: they wait for its work
/// while it is held.
pub struct Seat<'c> {
    convoy: &'c dyn Turns,
}

trait Turns {
    fn leave(&self);
    fn release(&self);
    fn take(&self);
}

impl Seat<'_> {
    /// Runs `f` without holding the device, as for work that may block,
    /// such as handing tokens to a client.
    pub fn away<T>(&self, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T {
        self.convoy.release();
        let out = f();
        self.convoy.take();
        out
    }
}

impl Drop for Seat<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.convoy.leave();
    }
}

casser RAD-1, Warm Start ni Convoy.

  control, fairness, priorité, annulation, backpressure.
- Décodage spéculatif : ordonnancement draft/verify, vérification d'arbre,
  rollback, réutilisation de KV.
- Concurrence Rust : threads/async, `Mutex`/`Condvar`, channels, atomics,
  `Send`/`Sync`, scoped threads, panic safety.
- Mémoire : dimensionnement du pool KV (N × contexte), fragmentation/défrag,
  mémoire unifiée, pinned host, paging des experts MoE, watchdog OOM.
- Graph capture/replay, multi-stream, recouvrement copies/calcul.
- Observabilité : TTFT, tok/s, p50/p99, cache hit, profondeur de file.

**Pourquoi ici** : `Engine.free` est un
`Mutex<Vec<(usize, Box<dyn Backend + 'a>)>>` : un pool de backends, une

requête ; `Convoy` mutualise des passes mais ne planifie pas ; le KV est

**KPI** : débit agrégé, p99, TTFT, cache hit, zéro régression d'exactitude.

The code reserves `context` per layer per slot at load; `default_slots` max 4; Vulkan 1 slot. A 32k context on a 16 GiB card can consume the entire GPU with 4 slots. Paged/unified KV is the fix. ## 0. Décision structurante : un seul backend complet par API

Le dépôt a aujourd'hui **deux couches par API GPU** :

- CUDA est éclaté entre `kinetic-cuda` (driver, noyaux, lanceurs) et
  `kinetic-models/src/cuda` (orchestration du modèle) ;
- Vulkan est éclaté entre `kinetic-vulkan` (loader, shaders, noyaux) et
  `kinetic-models/src/vulkan` (orchestration du modèle).

La cible est différente et plus simple :

> **Un seul backend complet par API GPU.** Tout CUDA vit dans `kinetic-cuda` :
> driver, noyaux, layouts, graphes, mémoire, exécution du modèle, capacités.
> Tout Vulkan vit dans `kinetic-vulkan`. Le CPU reste le chemin de référence :
> ses noyaux dans `kinetic-cpu`, son exécution générique dans `kinetic-models`.
> `kinetic-models` ne contient plus de code CUDA/Vulkan : il décrit les
> architectures, les blocs et les invariants, et expose une interface
> d'exécution **au niveau modèle** (charger, préfill, décoder, état de
> séquence, capacités), pas au niveau noyau.

Consolider ne signifie pas copier CUDA dans Vulkan. Chaque backend doit
offrir les mêmes **classes** de fonctionnalités — graphes/replay, attention
flash, MoE groupé, KV quantifié, multi-device — avec les mécanismes de son
API. La parité se juge en fonctionnalités, en exactitude et en mesures, pas
en lignes de code.

Les autres API (HIP, SYCL, WebGPU) sont des **backends de compatibilité** :
chacun est complet pour son API, mais n'est ajouté que lorsqu'une machine et
une CI peuvent le valider. Metal reste un chemin du backend Vulkan
(MoltenVK), pas un backend séparé. L'utilisateur n'en charge qu'un seul à
l'exécution, selon sa carte. On fournit le socle (trait, capacités, tests de
